journal_articles.title: Citron kinase activity controls alternative splicing events that drive prostate cancer growth.
journal_articles.abstract: Prostate cancer (CaP) remains a major cause of cancer death in men, underscoring the need for mechanistically novel therapies. We previously identified the action of the mitotic kinase citron (CIT) kinase as a key driver of CaP progression and promising therapeutic target, but selective CIT inhibitors are not available. We therefore asked whether a better understanding of the action of CIT substrates, which execute CIT kinase action in CaP cells, can lead to novel approaches and/or alternative targets to indirectly interfere with CIT's activity during CaP progression. In view of the enrichment in functions in alternative splicing among CIT substrates, we focus on the RNA splicing regulator THRAP3 as a representative substrate. Direct THRAP3 phosphorylation by CIT determined THRAP3's RNA binding to CIT-controlled pre-messenger RNA targets. Cross-linking and immunoprecipitation sequencing identified a subset of CIT-dependent THRAP3-bound genes that were preferentially involved in cell proliferation. THRAP3 RNA binding was enriched in genes that undergo alternative splicing during CaP progression. CIT-dependent THRAP3-bound transcripts stimulated the growth of CaP cell lines, xenografts, patient-derived organoids, and patient-derived xenograft (PDX)-derived organoids, whereas CIT-independent THRAP3-bound transcripts from the same gene did not. An antisense oligo that blocks THRAP3's recruitment to a CIT-dependent RNA binding site prevented the production of CIT- and THRAP3-dependent transcripts and inhibited the growth of cell lines and PDX-derived organoids representing different CaP stages and lineages but not of benign cells. Thus, CIT-mediated alternative splicing drives CaP progression, and its inhibition is a new therapeutic strategy in treatment-resistant CaP.

journal_articles.title: Deep learning reveals ecological decoupling and rate heterogeneity in Hymenoptera wing evolution.
journal_articles.abstract: Quantifying biomorphological evolution and integrating phenotypic data into large-scale ecological and evolutionary studies are often limited by the scalability, subjectivity, and poor interpretability of existing methods. We introduce HAIKA (Hierarchical Attention-based Interpretable K-dimensional Autoencoder), a self-supervised residual channel-attention autoencoder that extracts continuous morphological representations from unlabeled standardized images and highlights the image regions that contribute to those representations. Applied to insect forewings across broad pterygote lineages, HAIKA outperformed most baseline deep learning models and conventional descriptors in clustering, dimensionality reduction, and morphological embedding. When applied to Hymenoptera (i.e., ants, bees, and wasps), the HAIKA-derived continuous characters improved morphology-based phylogenetic reconstruction and illuminated the evolutionary dynamics of wing shape and venation. Our results reveal that wing morphological evolution in Hymenoptera proceeds at decoupled rates across shape and venation modules and is not consistently aligned with key ecological transitions such as parasitoidism or eusociality. HAIKA provides a scalable, image-based route for phenotypic analyses, broadly applicable across diverse taxa and to both 2D and 3D datasets.

journal_articles.title: Dishevelled-mediated clustering stabilizes Frizzled6 and Vangl2 to establish planar cell polarity in the mammalian skin.
journal_articles.abstract: Planar cell polarity (PCP) in epithelia is characterized by the polarized distribution of two opposing, membrane-associated PCP complexes across cell junctions. Transmembrane components of the PCP complex bridge cell junctions and organize into punctate, intercellular assemblies that exhibit a high degree of stability. Here, we define the contributions of the cytoplasmic PCP protein, Dishevelled (Dvl), in the submicrometer scale organization and stability of PCP complexes. Using endogenously tagged fluorescent PCP reporters in the embryonic mouse epidermis, we quantify PCP protein mobility and clustering during polarization. We find that as transmembrane proteins immobilize into puncta, Dvl2/3 coaccumulates with its transmembrane partner Frizzled 6 in a polarized manner and stabilizes clusters of PCP complexes. We identify a previously unknown function for the oligomerizing Dishevelled/Axin (DIX) domain of Dvl3, typically associated with Wnt signaling, in Dvl3 asymmetric localization. These observations underscore a role for Dvl oligomerization in assembly and stabilization of asymmetric PCP puncta.

journal_articles.title: Effects of probiotics on joint homeostasis and osteoarthritis: Development of microbe-gut-cartilage axis-on-a-chip.
journal_articles.abstract: Although emerging evidence implicates gut microbiome-cartilage cross-talk in the pathogenesis of osteoarthritis (OA), the most common joint disease, studying this microbe-gut-joint axis remains challenging due to limitations of animal models and conventional in vitro systems. Here, we report a microbe-gut-cartilage axis-on-a-chip (MGCAoC) that recreates tissue-specific microenvironments with oxygen gradients and physiological fluid shear. The computer simulation-optimized chip design generates an anoxic-oxic interface for the gut module and enables perfusion of probiotic metabolites to human cartilage organoids without cross-contamination. Multiomics profiling suggested that probiotic metabolites may promote cartilage anabolism, potentially involving PI3K and MAPK pathway, and this effect was associated with up-regulated collagen type II and aggrecan expression while suppressing metalloproteinases. In inflamed cartilage organoids, these metabolites were associated with reduced proinflammatory signaling while preserving matrix integrity. The chondroprotective effects were confirmed using cartilage organoids derived from patients with OA treated with identified metabolites. This MGCAoC enables mechanistic investigation of gut-joint axis physiology and provides a versatile preclinical tool for screening probiotic-based OA therapeutics.

journal_articles.title: Extracellular matrix-targeted TNC-scFv armoring enhances CAR T cell persistence and antitumor activity in solid tumors.
journal_articles.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor T cell (CAR T cell) therapy has shown limited efficacy in solid tumors, largely due to physical and immunosuppressive barriers imposed by the tumor microenvironment (TME). Tenascin-C (TNC), an extracellular matrix protein highly expressed in multiple solid malignancies, contributes to immune exclusion and T cell dysfunction. Here, we engineer an armored CAR T cell platform that locally targets the extracellular matrix by secreting a TNC-specific single-chain variable fragment (TNC-scFv) linked to conventional CAR architecture. TNC-scFv-armored CAR T cells exhibit enhanced cytotoxic activity, improved persistence, and reduced exhaustion in vitro and in xenograft tumor models. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis reveals that TNC targeting reprograms the TME toward a CD8+ T cell-enriched and functionally active immune landscape. In humanized tumor models, TNC-scFv-armored CAR T cells mediate robust antitumor responses with minimal systemic toxicity. This extracellular matrix-targeted armoring framework is compatible with additional immunomodulatory payloads, as illustrated by combinatorial armoring with interleukin-2, which further enhances efficacy while mitigating cytokine-associated toxicity. Together, these results establish extracellular matrix-directed armoring as a generalizable strategy to improve CAR T cell therapy for solid tumors.

journal_articles.title: From scrap to prime: Designing high-performance alloys from dirty feedstocks with machine learning.
journal_articles.abstract: Producing alloys from recycled metals via secondary synthesis can markedly cut energy use, greenhouse-gas emissions, and dependence on scarce, strategically important elements relative to primary routes. The central obstacle is the feedstock itself: Scrap is chemically heterogeneous and unpredictable, a "dirty" mix whose impurities typically embrittle materials. Conventional strategies address this challenge by diluting impurities through the addition of virgin material, thereby restricting scrap utilization, limiting microstructural design freedom, and undermining cost and sustainability benefits. Here, we introduce a fundamentally different, data-driven paradigm that deliberately reverses a five-millennia-old metallurgical injunction: Rather than purifying the alloy, we design the alloy to accommodate and exploit its contaminants. Using a model ductile iron representative of 120 million metric tons of heavily contaminated scrap, we couple experiments with deep-neural-network optimization to identify chemically robust, impurity-tolerant processing windows. The resulting "dirty" irons retain ductility and strength by integrating impurity effects into a purposeful microstructure, rather removing them. The approach achieves complete recyclability, an 8.1% reduction in manufacturing cost, and mechanical gains of up to 15.2% in ultimate tensile strength and 73.2% in elongation at fracture. Crucially, it overcomes the canonical strength-ductility trade-off while enabling far greater scrap utilization and material circularity. By endowing alloys with a practical "gene of scrap compatibility," this strategy reframes alloy design for a resource-constrained future and advances a mass-conserving circular economy for metals.

journal_articles.title: HPSC-derived mesenchymal stromal cells ameliorate murine autistic-like phenotypes through activating oxytocinergic neurons.
journal_articles.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heritable neurodevelopmental disorder marked by social deficits, repetitive behaviors, and psychiatric comorbidities. Despite its rising global prevalence, effective treatments remain elusive. Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) offer therapeutic promise for ASD, although their mechanisms are unclear. Here, we show that induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived MSCs alleviate anxiety, grooming, and social impairments in Shank3B knockout mice, a monogenic ASD model. Intravenously infused MSCs localize to the neurohypophysis, interface with oxytocin (OT)-producing neuron axons, and activate OT+ neurons in the paraventricular nucleus (PVN). MSC treatment also reduces autistic-like phenotypes in BTBR T + Itpr3tf/J mice, a model of idiopathic ASD, in an OT+ neuron-dependent manner. Mechanistically, prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) secreted by MSCs instigates the activation of OT+ neuron, while suppression of PGE2 production via short hairpin RNA (shRNA)-mediated knockdown of PTGS1 and PTGES diminishes their therapeutic efficacy. These findings reveal a mechanism whereby MSCs modulate OT+ neuroendocrine circuits to improve ASD-related behaviors.

journal_articles.title: Hydrogen isotopes reveal water leakage from the core.
journal_articles.abstract: Chemical heterogeneities in Earth's deep mantle may record either preserved primordial reservoirs or later core-mantle exchange, but distinguishing between these origins remains challenging. Hydrogen isotopes offer a sensitive tracer, yet whether magma ocean crystallization could generate a deuterium-depleted deep reservoir has not been quantitatively evaluated. Here, we use machine learning-accelerated path-integral simulations to determine equilibrium hydrogen isotope fractionation between silicate melt and bridgmanite, ringwoodite, and wadsleyite under magma ocean conditions. Incorporating these fractionation factors into a magma ocean crystallization model shows that mineral-melt fractionation is intrinsically weak, producing an essentially homogeneous D/H distribution in the primitive mantle. Magma ocean crystallization therefore cannot generate the extremely low δD values observed in some ocean island basalts. Combined with exceptionally high 3He/4He ratios, these signatures more plausibly reflect selective transfer of primordial volatiles from Earth's core, implying sustained volatile exchange across the core-mantle boundary.

journal_articles.title: Insights into temporal and spatial dynamics of short association fiber formation in the human fetal brain.
journal_articles.abstract: Short association fibers (SAFs) form the local scaffold of cortical connectivity and support early functional specialization. However, their development before birth remains largely unknown. Using fetal diffusion magnetic resonance imaging from the Developing Human Connectome Project and histology from the Zagreb Collection of human brains, we present an in utero reconstruction of SAF pathways in the human brain. We tracked their volumetric and microstructural developmental trajectories in 243 fetuses spanning a critical period of connectome formation. We found that SAFs emerge before sulcal folding, initially as flat, loosely arranged pathways along the subplate-white matter interface, and later reorganize into coherent U-shaped bundles. Their maturation followed a sensorimotor-to-association gradient, paralleling cortical development. Nonlinear, bundle-specific trajectories captured multiphasic maturation, with subplate dynamics preceding increases in axonal coherence and early myelination. These findings reveal how the brain's local wiring is established during prenatal development and provide insight into the origins of individual variability.

journal_articles.title: Macrophage- or neutrophil-expressed UPP1 drives tumor growth and immune suppression in the tumor microenvironment.
journal_articles.abstract: Uridine phosphorylase 1 (UPP1) has recently emerged as a metabolic regulator with critical roles in tumor cell biology. However, its expression pattern and functional significance in nonmalignant components of the tumor microenvironment (TME) remain largely unexplored. Here, we performed a comprehensive pan-cancer single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealing that UPP1 is highly expressed not only in tumor cells but also in tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) and neutrophils (TANs). Clinically, UPP1 expression in TAMs and TANs correlates with poor prognosis and diminished response to immunotherapy across multiple cancer types. Mechanistically, UPP1 up-regulation could be driven by NF-κB signaling. Functionally, UPP1 reprograms macrophages toward a tumor-promoting phenotype, characterized by enhanced glycolysis, ATP-adenosine signaling activation, and increased production of immunosuppressive cytokines such as granulocyte colony-stimulating factor. In neutrophils, UPP1 also supports TAN polarization, influences neutrophil extracellular trap release, and contributes to broad immunosuppressive remodeling. In vivo, targeting UPP1 in macrophages or neutrophils reprograms the immune landscape and restrains tumor progression. Together, our findings uncover a previously underappreciated role of UPP1 in nonmalignant immune populations and establish it as a key immune mediator within the TME, offering a potentially promising therapeutic target for enhancing antitumor immunity.

journal_articles.title: Phage-ICE tandems facilitate bacterial adaptation and antimicrobial resistance spread.
journal_articles.abstract: Phages and integrative and conjugative elements (ICEs) drive bacterial evolution, but how their interplay shapes bacterial adaptation and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) dissemination remains unclear. Here, we characterize phage-ICE tandems formed by site-specific accretion of phages and ICEs into cotransferable units. In Streptococcus, phage-encoded integrases (IntIEPhage) drive stress-inducible excision and circularization, after which ICE machinery mediates conduction of the tandem. When excision is impaired, phage and phage-ICE fragments disseminate by transformation and integrate via RecA-dependent homologous recombination (HR), providing a fail-safe route. This pathway enables cotransfer of flanking chromosomal DNA, generating length-variable integrations that remodel transcriptional programs and increase oxidative stress tolerance. A global screen identified 612 phage-ICE tandems across seven phyla and 135 species, including multidrug-resistant pathogens, with lineage-specific repertoires of AMR, virulence, and metabolic genes. Rather than a hybrid element, these structures represent functional interplay where prophages exploit ICE conjugation while facilitating mobilization of the composite region. By coupling excision, transfer, and recombination, phage-ICEs shape adaptation and accelerate AMR spread.

journal_articles.title: Plasmonic metasurface microfluidic accelerates redox reactions for rapid phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing.
journal_articles.abstract: Electron-accepting chain reactions play crucial roles in diagnostics for bacterial infections, from nucleic acid amplification for bacterial identification to metabolic assays for phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing. When coupled with redox mediators, these reactions can be interrogated using an electroanalytical method. We demonstrate kinetic acceleration of loop-mediated isothermal amplification-based identification and resazurin-based phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility profiling through enhanced electromagnetic fields and modulated hot electron injection at the multilayered plasmonic metasurface-fluidic interface. We systematically investigate rounded versus sharp-apex plasmonic architectures, quantifying near-field magnitude and decay to identify geometries that maximize kinetic amplification under electrochemical readout. This approach is further combined with machine learning-assisted Gaussian fitting to improve data quantification and interpretation. Across diverse bacterial species, we achieved rapid identification with no cross-reactivity and phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing without overnight culture. In a prospective pilot clinical study of urine specimens directly from patients with suspected urinary tract infections, we observe high accuracy and strong essential and categorical agreement with standard clinical microbiology assays for bacterial identification and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

journal_articles.title: SMCHD1 is a target for gene activation therapy to treat Prader-Willi syndrome.
journal_articles.abstract: Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS) is a neurodevelopmental disorder caused by loss of expression from the active paternal allele at an imprinted cluster on chromosome 15. Current treatments address individual symptoms rather than the underlying cause of disease. Because all patients preserve a normal but epigenetically silenced maternal copy of these genes, activation of this copy offers a potential disease-modifying therapy. Here, we investigated the epigenetic regulator SMCHD1. First, we demonstrated that SMCHD1 represses the PWS locus in both mice and humans, supporting its relevance as a therapeutic target. Second, we found that SMCHD1 represses the entire PWS locus in neural lineages, extending its previously known role beyond only part of the cluster. Deleting Smchd1 after early development in vivo activated PWS genes in disease-relevant mouse tissues including hypothalamus and improved phenotypes in a PWS mouse model. Despite broader genome-wide binding, postearly development targeting of SMCHD1 appeared remarkably safe, supporting its potential for gene activation therapy for PWS.

journal_articles.title: Targeting SUV39H2 exon skipping reverses resistance to CDK4/6 inhibitors via transcriptional activation of p21.
journal_articles.abstract: Cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 inhibitors (CDK4/6i) are standard therapies for estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer, but their efficacy is limited by drug resistance. While dysregulation of alternative splicing has been implicated in cancer progression, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we uncover a splicing-mediated mechanism whereby exon 2 inclusion in SUV39H2 drives its overexpression in CDK4/6i-resistant breast cancer cells. Clinically, elevated exon 2 inclusion in SUV39H2 correlates with poor prognosis in patients with breast cancer. Targeting SUV39H2 with gapmer antisense oligonucleotides or a methyltransferase inhibitor overcomes CDK4/6i resistance and reinstates therapy-induced senescence in breast cancer cells by reducing SUV39H2 expression or activity. Mechanistically, targeting SUV39H2 promotes transcriptional activation of senescence-associated secretory phenotype genes, including p21, through H3K9me3 removal at enhancer regions and subsequent chromatin opening at promoters. Our work unveils a splicing-mediated resistance mechanism and presents a potential synergistic drug target for CDK4/6i therapy.

preprints.title: A high-resolution protein-RNA binding atlas for structure-aware interaction prediction and post-transcriptional regulatory modeling
preprints.abstract: RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) control post-transcriptional gene expression by regulating RNA processing, localization, stability, and translation. However, our understanding of RNA regulation remains limited by the resolution, scale, and uniformity of available RBP binding maps. Here we introduce eclair CLIP (ecCLIP), a high-throughput CLIP-seq platform that combines endogenous protein tagging for uniform affinity capture with ligation-free library preparation to generate high-resolution RNA-protein binding profiles. We applied ecCLIP to 67 endogenously tagged RBPs in HEK293T cells, generating a high-quality transcriptome-scale atlas that recovered known binding preferences and captured post-transcriptional regulons linked to RNA half-life. To test the utility of the atlas, we incorporated ecCLIP into Borzuki, a Borzoi-derived sequence-to-function model trained on complementary RNA degradation, expression, CLIP, and Perturb-seq data. Inclusion of ecCLIP data improved RNA half-life prediction and assessment of 3' UTR variant effects on RNA stability, demonstrating that our atlas helps capture RNA dynamics. To directly model the cis-regulatory grammar underlying these RBP-RNA interactions, we developed Pythia, a structure-aware neural network architecture that incorporates context-free grammar-inspired fixed convolutions to explicitly encode RNA base-pairing features. Pythia predicted RBP binding from sequence and structural context and decomposed predictions into sequence- and structure-dependent components. We tested this decomposition for five RBPs using massively parallel reporter CLIP (MPRC) binding assays in cells, using synthetic RNA libraries containing mutations designed to preserve or disrupt predicted RNA structures across nominated binding sites. We used the same MPRC strategy to confirm allele-specific binding effects for variants prioritized by Pythia. Together, ecCLIP and Pythia provide a resource for structure-aware decoding of RNA-protein interaction grammar and interpretation of post-transcriptional regulatory variation.

preprints.title: High-throughput identification of chromatin-opening transcription factors
preprints.abstract: Cell fate transitions involve major changes to the chromatin landscape, some of which are thought to deepen the basin around a newly adopted cell state, stabilizing gene expression programs that might otherwise be transient. Transcription factors (TFs) are central to this process, binding a subset of their genome-wide motif occurrences to create accessible regions that can act as cell type-specific enhancers. However, apart from a few well-studied cases, it is not clear which of the ~1,600 mammalian TFs, when newly expressed, can directly or indirectly initiate newly accessible sites, nor why only some motif occurrences gain accessibility. Here, we applied pooled CRISPR activation (CRISPRa) to upregulate endogenous TFs to physiological levels in mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs). After screening guides targeting 240 developmental TFs for transcriptional response, we selected 60 and jointly profiled gene expression and chromatin accessibility in ~140,000 single cells. Some TFs (e.g. Cdx2, Sox10) appeared to initiate new accessibility on their own, predominantly at distal sites that are closed in mESCs but coincide with cell type-specific enhancers later in development. Others appeared to partner with "co-TFs", either by leveraging preexisting mESC heterogeneity (e.g. {uparrow}Grhl1 in Tfap2c+ mESCs [->] opening of sites bearing motifs for both), or by hierarchical activation (e.g. {uparrow}Sox7 [->] {uparrow}Gata6 [->] opening of sites bearing either or both motifs). Such dependencies shape which sites are used and which fates are reachable, and may explain the differential behavior of TFs with nearly identical consensus motifs. Thus, the capacity of a newly expressed TF to open chromatin strongly depends on the cell type, cell state and gene regulatory network it lands in. Charting these dependencies will inform how cell fate transitions are initiated in development, homeostasis and disease, and how to engineer them in silico, in vitro and in vivo.

preprints.title: Single-Cell Multimodal Profiling Reveals Maternal Diabetes-Nkx2-5 Interaction in Congenital Heart Disease in a Genetic Model Recapitulating Human Embryopathies
preprints.abstract: The etiological complexity of congenital heart disease (CHD) arises from the interaction between genetic and environmental factors. We hypothesized that environmental exposure could potentiate a genetic susceptibility, leading to an increased incidence of specific cardiac defects. To test this hypothesis, we used betaV59M+ female mice exhibiting severe hyperglycemia (>28 mmol/L) without dyslipidemia, a model we characterized that faithfully recapitulates human diabetic embryopathy. These females were crossed with males haploinsufficient for Nkx2-5, a transcription factor essential for cardiac development and implicated in human CHD. Our results show that the combination of genetic susceptibility and a hyperglycemic maternal environment (GxE) leads to a higher frequency and severity of cardiac malformations, including ventricular septal defects specifically involving the muscular septum, univentricular morphologies, and dilation with thinning of the myocardium. These structural abnormalities were associated with transcriptional changes affecting the contractile identity of the chamber myocardium. Single-nucleus multiomic profiling (snRNA-seq and snATAC-seq) of the E9.5 cardiac region revealed that the interaction between maternal diabetes and Nkx2-5 haploinsufficiency profoundly reshapes transcriptional and chromatin accessibility landscapes. These changes affect not only metabolic pathways, but also cell cycle progression in second heart field (SHF) progenitors, likely contributing to the observed structural cardiac defects. Multiomic integration further identifies a disrupted indirect Nkx2-5-Aldh1a2 regulatory axis in posterior SHF progenitors, while demonstrating that maternal diabetes selectively affects a restricted subset of Nkx2-5-dependent regulatory elements associated with cardiomyocyte maturation. Our findings establish a comprehensive single-cell multiomic resource that will facilitate the integration of human GWAS and other genomic datasets, enabling the identification and functional interpretation of disease-associated loci.

preprints.title: A cellular atlas of Astyanax mexicanus embryogenesis reveals principles of developmental microevolution
preprints.abstract: The evolution of development is the primary mechanism by which morphological and functional diversity is generated. Comparing the developmental trajectories of single cells in entire embryos across species can reveal how gene expression is conserved and varies, as well as the molecular mechanisms underlying how cell- and tissue-specific changes in developmental regulation generate phenotypic differences. However, this perspective has not addressed the mechanisms of small-scale developmental microevolution, i.e, in closely-related species or even within a single species. The fish Astyanax mexicanus, which comes in two forms adapted to distinct environments - the eyed, river-dwelling morph and the eyeless, cave-adapted morph - is a remarkable model with which to investigate the evolution of gene regulation in a single species. Here, we generated and analyzed a single-nucleus RNA-seq atlas of the development of the two Astyanax morphs, from gastrula to swimming larva. Despite extensive changes in gene expression observed in the eight examined stages, for both ubiquitously-expressed and tissue-specific genes, and in both embryonic and extra-embryonic tissues, the temporal progression of cavefish and surface fish cells was similar in ordinal regression-based pseudotime models using 20-100 core genes. However, transcriptome-wide comparisons of gene expression waves revealed massive heterochronic shifts. In cavefish, some tissues had a majority of genes lagging behind in their transcriptional dynamics (e.g. the optic region), while in others, a majority of genes had accelerated dynamics (e.g. the mesoderm), or else, an equivalent number of genes were found in either category (e.g. the endoderm). Furthermore, cell fate acquisition and differentiation were variably affected in different cavefish lineages, with delays of ~6 hours in the retina, ~2 hours in the axial mesoderm and ~none in the extra-embryonic enveloping layer. Thus, cavefish embryos progress as a mosaic of different tissues, or modules, each following its own transcriptional tempo. Because gene expression differential regulation and time shifts were more prevalent in the early stages and gradually diminished throughout development, we propose that cavefish embryos initially undergo strong decanalisation before becoming re-canalized in line with the shared Astyanax developmental program.

preprints.title: Decoding super-enhancer regulatory grammar and pathogenic gain-of-function variants directly from DNA sequence
preprints.abstract: Super-enhancers (SEs) drive cell-identity gene expression, yet their identification relies on epigenomic profiling (e.g., H3K27ac ChIP-seq), precluding discovery in unprofiled cellular states and leaving their underlying sequence grammar unknown. Here, we present Borzoi-SE, a deep learning framework built upon the genomic transformer Borzoi that formulates SE discovery as hierarchical, cell-type-resolved genomic object detection directly from long-range sequence across 90 human lineages. Base-resolution attribution recovers lineage-defining master transcription factors across cell types. Within SEs shared across lineages, it reveals lineage-dependent motif usage, suggesting that the same regulatory regions can support distinct cell-type-specific programs. Using in silico ablation, Borzoi-SE decoded the functional hierarchy of the {beta}-globin super-enhancer, prioritizing hypersensitive site 2 (HS2) as the dominant constituent, which we experimentally verified via CRISPR interference. Trained without variant-effect labels, Borzoi-SE identified gain-of-super-enhancer variants in different tissues. At the CHRM2 locus, a single-nucleotide variant created a de novo glucocorticoid receptor (GR) motif that recruited activated GR and potentiated adjacent MEF2 regulatory syntax, nucleating a cardiac super-enhancer. Orthogonal multi-omics and population-genetic evidence linked this variant to increased CHRM2 expression and variation in resting heart rate and PR-interval duration. Borzoi-SE establishes a general framework for decoding SE regulatory grammar and prioritizing causal non-coding variants directly from sequence.

preprints.title: Autonomous Dampening of Wnt Signaling Selects Zebrafish Spinal Cord Progenitors for an Oligodendrocyte Fate
preprints.abstract: Nervous system development relies on coordinated formation of neurons and glia from neural progenitor cells (NPCs). During spinal cord development, NPCs in the pMN domain of the ventral spinal cord produce motor neurons followed by oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs), a subset of which differentiate as oligodendrocytes, the myelinating cell of the vertebrate central nervous system. Whereas prior research has outlined an extensive gene regulatory network driving oligodendrocyte lineage cell differentiation, less is known about the mechanisms that specify NPCs for oligodendrocyte fate. To elucidate these mechanisms, our lab recently generated a single-cell RNA sequencing and single-cell ATAC sequencing multi-omics dataset from the zebrafish spinal cord. The dataset identified a molecularly distinct subset of NPCs that appear fated to the oligodendrocyte lineage, which we refer to as pre-OPCs. Our data revealed that pre-OPCs are enriched for RNAs encoding factors that antagonize Wnt signaling, such as barhl2 and cachd1. The chromatin regions associated with these genes are highly accessible in pre-OPCs, suggesting that their expression is developmentally regulated. Using confocal light microscopy to visualize expression of a Wnt-responsive transgenic reporter, we found that Wnt signaling is downregulated in the spinal cord immediately prior to OPC specification. To explore how modulation of Wnt signaling influences OPC specification, we pharmacologically inhibited or activated Wnt signaling immediately prior to OPC specification. These experiments revealed that embryos treated with a Wnt inhibitor produced excess OPCs whereas those treated with a Wnt agonist had a deficit of OPCs. Additionally, CRISPR/Cas9 targeted mutations of barhl2 and cachd1 impaired OPC production. Finally, we identified wnt4b as a ventral source of Wnt and determined that loss of wnt4b enhances OPC specification. Together, our studies reveal pre-OPC modulation of ventral Wnt signaling as a mechanism of OPC specification in the spinal cord.

preprints.title: DNA methylation-based prediction of differentiation state at cell-type resolution reveals an age-associated epigenetic mesenchymal drift
preprints.abstract: Quantifying the differentiation state of cells is an important task in regenerative medicine, cellular reprogramming and in elucidating how differentiation hierarchies are altered in aging and disease. For DNA methylation data (DNAm) there is however an accute shortage of methods for quantifying differentiation state. Here we use machine learning to build EpiDiff, a predictor of differentiation that yields a continuous absolute differentiation index (DI) when applied to a DNAm sample. We extensively validate EpiDiff in single-cells, sorted cells and bulk tissue, as well as in in-vitro differentiation, organoid, reprogramming and cellular rejuvenation experiments. In mixed samples, EpiDiff measures the extent of differentiation across all cellular lineages. In sorted cell populations, we find that DI increases with age and, underpinning this increase, we discover that many cell-types undergo a developmental epigenetic drift that is most prominent towards the mesenchymal lineage. When applied to normal-tissues, EpiDiff is predictive of carcinogenic exposure and cancer risk. In summary, EpiDiff is a unique, general and versatile tool that can accurately quantify the global differentiation state of a DNAm sample with broad applicability to many disciplines.

preprints.title: Disrupted chromatin architecture blocks B lymphopoiesis in Down syndrome
preprints.abstract: Human fetal haematopoiesis requires developmental potential to be encoded before lineage identity becomes transcriptionally apparent, but whether three-dimensional genome architecture provides such information is unknown. Here we develop ChromE-seq, a scalable single-cell assay that jointly profiles chromatin conformation and transcription, and integrate it with chromatin accessibility and DNA methylation to generate a multimodal atlas of ~400,000 haematopoietic cells from disomic and trisomy 21 (T21) human fetal liver. Chromatin contacts frequently preceded lineage-specific transcription or persisted after transcription declined, revealing 3D chromatin priming and memory. Unexpectedly, B-lineage and erythroid differentiation followed opposing architectural trajectories, with progressive loss and gain of chromatin connectivity, respectively. T21 disproportionately disrupted B-lineage architecture, redistributed interactions towards shorter genomic distances and weakened an EBF1-centred regulatory circuit. Deletion of a T21-sensitive EBF1 loop anchor reproduced the CLP-to-B-progenitor bottleneck observed in T21. These findings establish 3D genome architecture as an organizing layer of human fetal haematopoiesis that links developmental potential with lineage-specific vulnerability to genomic perturbation.

preprints.title: Paired single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomics of the lung adenocarcinoma invasion sequence reveal niche domains and candidate reversal compounds
preprints.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) develops through a defined morphological sequence from atypical adenomatous hyperplasia (AAH) to invasive adenocarcinoma, but the transcriptional programmes accompanying this transition have mostly been characterised in bulk tissue or in tumour tissue alone. We profiled paired samples spanning the full sequence by single-nucleus RNA sequencing (413,697 nuclei, 23 patients) and spatial transcriptomics (56 Visium sections, 25 patients), asking how the transcriptional state of the tissue changes as invasion proceeds and whether that state can be reversed in silico by known perturbations. The atlas resolves into 39 second-level subtypes and the tissue into seven recurring niche-domain archetypes (K* = 7), six of which are ordinary lung structures and only one of which is restricted to invasive disease. A confound then shaped the remaining analyses: domain identity, marker stability and the apparent stage-dependence of the spatial programmes all scale with sequencing depth, and depth is in these sections a proxy for tissue density rather than a purely technical artefact (rho=-0.89 between a domain's depth and the fraction of its markers surviving depth matching). Several apparently positive results disappeared once depth was matched. The invasive domain's ECM/interstitial identity survives that check: within patients the fibroblast ECM programme is higher in invasive disease in 20 of 22 paired cases (P=0.0033 against random gene sets), and the result is unchanged when the genes added by hand are removed and under every leave-one-out variant. Querying a patient-paired disease axis against the LINCS compound library with three scoring schemes returned 34 compounds in common, dominated by PI3K/mTOR inhibitors, with a split-half reproducibility of rho=0.962 against a permutation null of +/-0.045 and an agreement of rho=0.735 between a single-cell-derived and a spatially derived axis. A positive control, the recovery of known regulators of an official benchmark (TBXT ranked 1st of 8,450), establishes that the pipeline recovers true positives, so the negative results reported here are properties of the data rather than of the method. Those negatives are stated explicitly: single-cell copy-number inference produced no usable malignant/non-malignant separator, the cohort-level spatial copy-number difference did not survive depth matching, a developmental trajectory ran opposite to that of the source study, gene-level prediction returned no signal on the pooled axis and only one perturbation survives compartment-wise gating, and a ligand-level analysis produced no usable pair.

preprints.title: DEPICT enables sample-centric therapeutic prioritization across evolving and spatially heterogeneous tumor states
preprints.abstract: Accurate treatment selection remains a major challenge in precision oncology because tumors with similar genomic alterations can respond differently to therapy. Most drug-response models evaluate individual drugs or drug-sample pairs, whereas clinical decision-making requires therapies to be prioritized within each tumor context. Here we present DEPICT (Drug Efficacy Prediction via Integrated ConText), a sample-centric deep learning framework that reframes drug-response prediction as the relative prioritization of therapies within an individual tumor context. DEPICT integrates transcriptomic and mutational features with prior alteration-therapy relationship and was trained on 231,880 cell line-drug pairs comprising 941 cancer cell lines and 289 compounds. Without retraining, DEPICT retained predictive performance in independently profiled cell lines, experimentally induced drug-resistant states and matched primary lung tumors and patient-derived organoids. Representations learned exclusively from bulk pharmacogenomic data further captured progressive drug-response states at single-cell resolution and outperformed existing single-cell drug-response inference methods. Applied to spatial transcriptomic data, DEPICT resolved clone-associated therapeutic heterogeneity within individual lung tumors, and predicted regional differences were recapitulated in matched multiregional organoid drug-response assays. These findings establish sample-centric therapeutic prioritization as a transferable strategy for modeling dynamic and spatially heterogeneous drug vulnerabilities across biological scales.

last_author.name: Zheng, C.
last_author.affiliation: Peking University

preprints.title: From Closed-Set Annotation to In-Context Discovery: Biologically Grounded LLMs for Cellular Profiling
preprints.abstract: Tumour heterogeneity reflects both cellular identity (lineage) and state (active transcriptional programs), yet computational methods generally analyse these axes separately. We introduce CellScribe, a generative framework that conditions a pretrained language model on frozen single cell foundation model embeddings through AdaLN adapters, enabling one shared model to generate an ontology- grounded cell type or a quantified meta-program profile. Supervised multitask fine- tuning produces fine grained typing across hundreds of cell types and outperforms generative and retrieval baselines on meta-program identification under study-holdout evaluation. We further train the model with reinforcement learning, scoring its generations against cell ontology distance and meta-program agreement, so that they align with biological knowledge rather than token agreement. To identify new cell types not present in the supervised training data, we post-train the model to read several labelled example cells in a single context, each conditioning its own text span, and infer the type of a query cell through in-context learning. CellScribe thus unifies cell identity and state in one generative interface, grounds both in biological structure, and identifies cell types outside the supervised vocabulary.

preprints.title: SORT disentangles multilevel gene programs across heterogeneous spatial transcriptomic atlases
preprints.abstract: Understanding how transcriptional programs are organized across biological contexts is essential for deciphering tissue development, disease progression, and species-specific adaptations. Spatial transcriptomic atlases spanning patients, developmental stages, and species provide an opportunity to resolve gene expression programs (GEPs) that are sample-specific, group-shared, or region-associated, yet strong sample-specific variation can obscure weaker shared programs. Here we introduce SORT, a matrix factorization framework that jointly recovers multilevel GEPs and their spatial activities, using orthogonality to reduce program redundancy and graph total variation to preserve spatial boundaries. In simulations with strong patient variation, SORT more accurately recovered patient-specific, subtype-shared, and region-associated programs than existing methods. Across 108 pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma sections, SORT resolved tumor and stromal programs with distinct and overlapping activities and linked these activities to survival across four external cohorts. In a cross-species cerebellar atlas, SORT distinguished conserved layer-associated programs from species-specific activity variation. Across eight stages of mouse organogenesis, SORT revealed GEPs with anatomical redeployment and graded spatial activity, as well as stage-dependent local co-deployment of distinct programs.

last_author.name: Zhang, S.

preprints.title: Single-Cell Proteo-Transcriptomic Profiling Uncovers Post-Translational Regulatory Layers in Human Hematopoiesis
preprints.abstract: Background: Hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) have the unique ability to produce all mature cell types in the blood and understanding the mechanisms governing their differentiation and renewal is a driving question in stem cell biology. While single-cell RNA sequencing has transformed our view of human hematopoiesis, mRNA abundance represents an incomplete proxy for functional cell states. Here, we apply single-cell multimodal profiling to simultaneously measure 280 surface and intracellular protein targets alongside whole transcriptomes within individual adult human hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells. Results: By directly coupling modalities within single cells, we show that protein-RNA correlations peak dynamically in transitioning intermediate progenitors across lineages, consistent with pervasive post-transcriptional mechanics underlying lineage choice. Furthermore, key transcription factor proteins maintain multilineage co-expression longer into commitment than their transcripts, demarcating a possible window of fate decision reversibility. Moreover, low and flat CTNNB1 mRNA levels mask late-erythroid {beta}-catenin protein enrichment, apparently pairing with E-cadherin expression and suggesting post-translational stabilization at the cell membrane. Conclusions: This dataset enables the observation of translational dynamics and RNA-protein relationships throughout the differentiation landscape at an unprecedented level of granularity. Together, our findings demonstrate that transcriptomics alone misses fundamental regulatory programs, establishing single-cell proteo-transcriptomics as a powerful tool for decoding human stem cell fate.

last_author.name: Wilson, N. K.
last_author.affiliation: University of Cambridge

preprints.title: Meis2 is required for GABAergic amacrine cell survival in the developing retina.
preprints.abstract: Amacrine cells (ACs) are the most diverse neuron in the retina, with more than sixty different subtypes, each contributing to the detection of specific visual features. Despite their importance in visual feature detection, the genetic basis for this diversity is still not well understood. Recent single-cell transcriptomic datasets have identified several potential genes that may regulate cellular diversity, but the underlying mechanisms have not been investigated. For example, the transcription factor Meis2 is selectively expressed in the GABAergic subclass of ACs. In this study, we focused on how Meis2 regulates the development of GABAergic ACs. We hypothesized that Meis2 is required for specification and survival of GABAergic ACs. To test this, we used the Meis2 conditional knockout mouse (Meis2-CKO) where Meis2 was deleted from either the entire retina or specifically from AC precursor cells. The deletion of Meis2 led to a ~60% reduction in total GABAergic ACs in the retina. This loss of GABAergic ACs occurred only after postnatal day 5 (P5), suggesting Meis2 is not required for early specification but may be required for survival. To further investigate cell death and survival, we quantified cleaved caspase-3 positive cells in the retina at several developmental timepoints. In Meis2-CKO mice, we found an increase in cleaved caspase-3 immunolabeling at P5 and P6 timepoints coinciding with the reduction of GABAergic ACs. Further analysis of GABAergic AC subtypes demonstrated a subtype-specific cell death in Meis2-CKO retinas. For example, the total number of dopaminergic (TH) ACs were significantly reduced, whereas starburst (ChAT) ACs remained unchanged. These findings suggest that Meis2 is important for the survival of a subset of GABAergic AC subtypes in the mammalian retina. In addition, Meis2 may control the expression of specific survival factors that prevent apoptosis during developmental cell death in the retina.

last_author.name: Kerstein, P. C.
last_author.affiliation: Purdue University

preprints.title: Spatiotemporal AI modeling of gene regulation and variant effects in the developing human brain
preprints.abstract: Understanding how genetic variation shapes gene regulation in the developing human brain remains a central challenge in neuroscience, particularly in transient cell types and developmental stages where data are limited. We present Seal, an interpretable AI transfer learning framework for genome-based modeling of gene expression and variant effects with spatiotemporal resolution across 26 brain regions, 30 cell types, and seven developmental stages. Seal predictions enable characterization of both germline and somatic brain variants, and provide mechanistic interpretation by linking sequence variants to transcriptional regulators in spatiotemporal context. Applying Seal to genome-wide association studies, we identify cell types and developmental windows relevant to neuropsychiatric disease risk, revealing shared and distinct regulatory architectures across six neuropsychiatric conditions that align with clinical trajectories. In the Simons Simplex Collection autism cohort whole genome data, Seal uncovers a significant burden of de novo regulatory variants in transient fetal excitatory neurons, revealing a cell-type and developmentally specific regulatory burden. By connecting genetic variation to spatiotemporal regulatory programs, Seal offers a general framework for uncovering mechanisms of human brain development and disease.

preprints.title: Concurrent de novo inference of cell types and gene regulatory networks with NetMap
preprints.abstract: Existing methods for GRN inference based on single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) data typically require prior cell type calling and then infer GRNs at cell type resolution. This risks propagation of errors from cell annotation to GRN inference. Moreover, it makes existing methods blind to regulatory programs that are shared between different cell types, as well as to subtle differences in regulatory activity between cells of the same type. To address these limitations, we present NetMap, a pipeline that jointly infers cell-level GRNs and clusters cells based on shared regulatory programs, combining state-of-the-art single-cell autoencoders and explainable artificial intelligence methods. NetMap outperforms existing methods on synthetic data with a known ground-truth GRN and is able to reliably detect biologically plausible regulons on real data. Moreover, requiring only a small set of user-provided marker genes, NetMap can be used for GRN structure-informed probabilistic cell type assignment. We demonstrate the utility of this approach using PBMC data, where we achieve near perfect clustering and cell type recovery performance compared with manually created cell type labels. Finally, we applied NetMap to a data set with naive, activated and exhausted T-cells, and were able to verify that NetMap retrieves relevant T-cell state signatures from the data, with two approaches. NetMap can be installed as a python package from https://github.com/bionetslab/netmap and is compatible with the scverse system. Scripts to reproduce our results can be found at https://github.com/bionetslab/netmap-evaluation.

preprints.title: Single-nucleus multi-omics reveals reversible molecular signatures in skeletal muscle of patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
preprints.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a complex systemic syndrome characterized by severe exercise intolerance. In addition to cardiac dysfunction, abnormalities in peripheral skeletal muscle are key contributors to reduced exercise capacity in HFpEF. Multiple studies show that exercise training and caloric restriction improve exercise capacity and quality of life in HFpEF patients. To map the HFpEF-associated molecular signatures in skeletal muscle and the effect of lifestyle intervention, we generated single-nucleus (sn) multiome (joint snRNA-seq and snATAC-seq) profiles of 140 biopsies. Our study included 95 individuals: 25 healthy controls and 70 HFpEF patients, of whom 45 had paired biopsies collected before and after a supervised diet and exercise intervention. From 132,568 nuclei, we resolved 15 skeletal muscle cell types and identified HFpEF-specific remodeling, including type 1 fiber and pericyte depletion and type 2x fiber enrichment, reflecting the cellular basis of exercise intolerance. Transcriptional changes in HFpEF muscle indicated dysregulation of metabolic pathways, stress-responsive programs, cytoskeletal integrity, and calcium signaling. Transcription factor (TF) motifs enriched in differentially accessible chromatin corresponded to concordantly differentially expressed TF-genes, revealing coordinated regulatory programs underlying these changes. Importantly, HFpEF-related changes in both chromatin accessibility and transcription were partially reversible following diet and exercise. Integrative multiomic velocity analyses revealed increased coordinated repression in both chromatin accessibility and transcription of calcium handling genes in HFpEF. HFpEF-linked chromatin was enriched for HF and cardiometabolic GWAS signals, and cross-modal analyses further nominated candidate causal variants and effector genes linking genetic risk to peripheral muscle dysfunction in HFpEF. Together, these findings highlight the molecular mechanisms underlying skeletal muscle remodeling in HFpEF and identify pathways responsive to lifestyle interventions.

last_author.name: Parker, S.

preprints.title: The dark transcriptome mouse organogenesis cell atlas
preprints.abstract: Single-cell atlases have transformed our understanding of mammalian tissue biology, yet the diverse noncoding "dark transcriptome" remains largely uncharted. Here, we present the Dark Transcriptome Mouse Organogenesis Cell Atlas (DT-MOCA), comprising 276,455 cells across embryonic days 11 to 18 and jointly capturing protein-coding transcripts and five major classes of noncoding RNAs through single-nucleus total RNA sequencing, establishing the first comprehensive catalog of noncoding RNAs across major cell types and developmental lineages. We found that long noncoding RNA and microRNA profiles distinguished major cell types and developmental lineages with resolution comparable to messenger RNA, whereas transfer RNA, small nuclear RNA, and small nucleolar RNA programs were less cell type-discriminative and more broadly shared. We further resolve noncoding RNA expression patterns as lineage-specific, temporally modulated, or coordinately regulated by cell identity and developmental stage. We observed that temporally regulated long noncoding RNAs were evolutionarily younger than those associated with cell identity. We further generate a catalog of the change of noncoding RNAs cross all 11 major developmental trajectories. It revealed lineage-specific coordination between transfer RNA supply and codon demand during musculoskeletal organogenesis as well as dynamic microRNA and small nucleolar RNA programs during the central nervous system development. We observed microRNAs converge on regulators of proliferation and gliogenesis and shared induction of Snord116 defining a developmental window relevant to Prader Willi syndrome. Together, this atlas provides a comprehensive catalog of the developmental dark transcriptome and reveals how noncoding RNA programs are organized across cell identity, developmental time, and lineage progression.

last_author.name: Fan, R.
last_author.affiliation: Yale University

preprints.title: A single epigenetic repressor controls opposing developmental tempos in human neural and cranial neural crest lineages
preprints.abstract: The precise timing of lineage specification is essential for embryonic development, yet the epigenetic mechanisms enforcing human developmental tempo remain poorly understood. Heterozygous loss-of-function variants in ZNF462 cause Weiss-Kruszka syndrome (WKS), a pleiotropic disorder characterized by neurodevelopmental delays and craniofacial dysmorphisms. Here, we show that ZNF462 acts as an epigenetic gatekeeper that coordinates human developmental tempo across divergent lineages by repressing cell lineage-specific gene enhancers. In human embryonic stem cells (hESCs), ZNF462 maintains self-renewal by recruiting the G9A/GLP histone methyltransferase complex to silence primate-specific retrotransposon-derived enhancers. Upon neural lineage commitment, ZNF462 redirects to hominoid-specific LTR5_Hs elements and divergent lineage-specific enhancer programs, where its loss produces opposing kinetics. In neural progenitor cells (NPCs), ZNF462 enforces G9A/GLP-dependent repression of ZIC-driven neural enhancers, and loss of this repression traps NPCs in a progenitor state, slowing cortical neurogenesis without impairing terminal neurogenic capacity. In neural crest cells (NCCs), ZNF462 targets repressive chromatin to silence SOX9 family-driven enhancers. Here, ZNF462 haploinsufficiency triggers premature activation of definitive NCC specifiers, accelerating differentiation. These findings establish that a single repressor can simultaneously decelerate and accelerate developmental tempo by gating lineage-specific enhancers, placing Weiss-Kruszka syndrome into the emerging class of human developmental timing disorders.

preprints.title: Cerberus: bidirectional state space blocks improve accuracy and efficiency of regulatory sequence models
preprints.abstract: Sequence-to-function models predict regulatory activity and variant effects from DNA sequence alone, and leading models such as Borzoi compute long-range interactions with self-attention. The reference genome caps unique training sequences, and new assays add labels, not sequences. This constraint favors architectures that learn more from limited sequence diversity. We compared long-range blocks with the rest of the architecture and the training data held fixed, replacing Borzoi's transformer blocks with Hydra, a bidirectional state space block built on Mamba-2. Hydra blocks ran 5.7-fold faster on 8,192-token inputs, and models built on them predicted binned coverage on held-out sequences and classified fine-mapped eQTLs more accurately. Hydra's linear cost in sequence length let us run the blocks at 32 bp resolution and remove the U-net decoder, leaving a convolution-SSM model smaller and more accurate than the one it replaced. Scaling this architecture up on an augmented track collection produced Cerberus, an ensemble of eight models over 786 kb of input. We evaluated it on GTEx v11 fine-mapped eQTL, sQTL, and paQTL benchmarks with negatives matched on allele frequency, gene expression, and phenotype-specific positional annotations to reduce confounding by these properties. Cerberus is more accurate than Borzoi on all three phenotypes, 0.692 versus 0.668 mean eQTL AUPRC across 48 tissues, and estimates eQTL effect sizes better, 0.379 versus 0.321 Spearman $\rho$. Against AlphaGenome, it trades leads in eQTL classification, ahead on variants 3 to 100 kb from the transcription start site and behind in coding sequence and within 3 kb. Interpretation of the trained blocks shows interaction range growing with block depth, from a 0.9 kb median half-life in the first block to 79 kb in the seventh, and the deepest heads anchoring on promoters, enhancers, and CTCF peaks. We release the models, the training data, the training and evaluation code, and the benchmark sets, supporting variant scoring and transfer learning.

preprints.title: DeSPA uncovers genes with cross-state spatial pattern remodeling and coordinated spatial programs across multi-slice spatial transcriptomics atlases
preprints.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics increasingly generates multi-slice atlases spanning developmental, regenerative, and disease-associated states. Identifying genes with spatial pattern remodeling across these states is essential for understanding tissue reorganization and the underlying gene programs, yet few existing methods systematically detect such changes while accounting for variation among replicate slices. Here we introduce DeSPA, a statistical framework that models gene-specific spatial variation within each slice using a linear mixed model, tests for cross-state remodeling by aggregating evidence across replicate slices, and organizes identified genes into interpretable spatial co-expression modules that reveal coordinated spatial programs. Simulations show that DeSPA achieves high power while controlling the false discovery rate under inter-slice heterogeneity. In mouse embryogenesis, it recovers programs linked to extracellular matrix organization, muscle formation, neural development, and erythrocyte development. In diabetic testis, it reveals disruption of a late-spermatid spatial program consistent with known spermatogenic dysfunction, while maintaining stable gene rankings under coordinate rotation. In axolotl brain, regeneration preserves a developmental-like biosynthetic backbone but reorganizes it into regeneration-specific modules. Across two mouse intracerebral hemorrhage models, DeSPA resolves a conserved spatial injury program alongside model-specific synaptic and tissue-response programs. Together, these findings establish DeSPA as a scalable and interpretable framework for detecting spatial pattern remodeling and resolving coordinated spatial programs across diverse biological states.

last_author.name: Zhang, S.
last_author.affiliation: Fudan University

preprints.title: Dysregulation of epithelial differentiation architecture underlies field cancerization in head and neck cancer
preprints.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) has exceptionally high recurrence rates, exceeding 50%, contributing to mortality and morbidity. This recurrence rate is proposed to be due to field cancerization, a phenomenon where tumor-adjacent "field" tissue that appears histologically normal harbors molecular changes that prime it for subsequent tumor growth. Current models attribute field cancerization to shared driver mutations between tumors and adjacent at-risk tissue, but this assumption has never been directly tested. To comprehensively characterize this phenomenon, we profiled patient-matched tumor, normal-adjacent field (NAF), contralateral normal, and blood samples from HPV-negative HNSCC patients using whole genome sequencing, targeted driver gene sequencing, single-nucleus multiome profiling, spatial transcriptomics and functional proliferation assays. While histologically normal NAF tissues did harbor expanded mutant clones, these mutations rarely overlapped with paired tumors and were not shared across patients, suggesting molecular features beyond mutations are altered in NAF. Single-cell multiomics revealed that NAF epithelium loses its normal organizational hierarchy: basal stem cell markers persist in differentiated cells, while terminal differentiation programs fail to activate, with reconfiguration of both gene regulatory networks and cell-cell interactions. Proliferating cells appeared in tissue layers normally restricted to post-mitotic cells, a pattern typically seen only in overt dysplasia. Within this disrupted hierarchy, a distinct epithelial state arose in NAF that expressed both normal epithelial and tumor-associated markers, which we localized to the parabasal layers using immunofluorescence and spatial transcriptomics. Together, our findings demonstrate that field cancerization operates through epithelial hierarchy disorganization that disrupts differentiation, generates cells with tumor-like features, and may create a permissive environment for the expansion of cancer-associated mutations, all within tissue that appears histologically normal.

preprints.title: Early-onset spontaneous murine mammary tumors show increased lymphocyte representation and reduced MHC antigen presentation
preprints.abstract: Simple Summary Not all breast tumors behave the same way, and part of the reason may be inherited rather than caused by the tumor itself. Using mice that carry the same cancer-causing HER2/neu gene but differ in genetic background, we found that introduction of the PWK/PhJ genetic background was associated with tumors that appeared about a month earlier. These early tumors contained a larger proportion of immune cells, including T and B cells, but the T-cell population showed reduced expression of genes associated with cytotoxic activity. At the same time, the tumors had lower levels of proteins and genes that let the immune system recognize tumor cells, alongside higher levels of structural proteins that can make tissue stiffer and easier for cancer to invade. These findings suggest that genetic background shapes not only how quickly breast tumors arise but also how well the immune system can recognize them, a distinction that may matter for future immune-based treatments. Background/Objectives: Genetic background modifies cancer risk and phenotype in humans, but its influence on the tumor immune microenvironment and antigen-presentation machinery in ErbB2 (HER2/neu)-driven breast cancer is not well defined. We used a genetically diverse mouse cross to test whether the wild-derived PWK/PhJ background alters immune representation and antigen presentation in a NeuT model of HER2/neu-positive breast cancer. Methods: Previously, quantitative trait locus (QTL) mapping using Diversity Outbred mice and r/qtl2 identified candidate loci driving tumor onset and growth. The wild-derived PWK/PhJ genetic background was predicted to harbor genes that regulated early onset of HER2/neu-driven tumors. BALB NeuT and (BALBxPWK) F1 NeuT female mice were monitored twice weekly for spontaneous mammary tumor onset and growth. Tumor immune composition was profiled by single-cell RNA sequencing. Protein abundance was measured by data-independent acquisition proteomics in formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tumor tissue (n=5 per genotype). Single-nucleus multiome (RNA + ATAC), bulk RNA-seq, and H3K27ac datasets from the same strain comparison were analyzed for focused MHC II cross-layer analyses. Results: As predicted, (BALBxPWK) F1 NeuT mice developed tumors significantly earlier than the parental BALB NeuT mice (10 vs. 15 weeks of age; p < 0.0001). In the scRNA-seq dataset, F1 tumors showed greater representation of Cd3e-expressing T cells and a Cd79a-expressing B-cell population not detected in BALB NeuT tumors, and a distinct neutrophil cluster; F1 T cells also showed lower expression of the cytotoxicity-associated genes Tox, Ltk, Nkg7, and Gzmb relative to BALB NeuT tumor-infiltrating T cells. Proteomics identified 46 differentially abundant proteins (25 higher, 21 lower in F1), with coordinate down-regulation of Stat1, Tapbp, Parp9, and Dtx3l alongside MHC class I and II proteins and up-regulation of extracellular-matrix and elastic-fiber proteins. Focused cross-layer analysis showed lower whole-tumor expression of a Stat1/MHC II-associated gene set together with reduced epithelial chromatin accessibility at selected regions near Cd74 and H2-Aa. Conclusions: The PWK/PhJ genetic background is associated with earlier HER2-driven tumor onset, greater lymphocyte proportion, and reduced activity of a STAT1-associated antigen-presentation program despite similar post-onset tumor growth kinetics.

last_author.name: Jacob, J. B.
last_author.affiliation: Michigan State University

preprints.title: Random mtDNA mutagenesis maps genotype-phenotype associations across metabolic contexts and lineages
preprints.abstract: Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) mutations cause inherited disease, accumulate with age, and recur in tumors, yet their effects remain unresolved because existing models interrogate one engineered allele at a time. We developed mtDIVE, a random C[->]T mutagenesis platform for pooled mitochondrial forward genetics in human epithelial cells and zebrafish embryos. mtDIVE generates genotypes ranging from single substitutions to >100 mutations per molecule, impairs respiration, and causes lineage-specific developmental delay. Coupling single-cell transcriptomics with mtDNA genotyping revealed that selection on mutant genomes and their transcriptional consequences depend on metabolic state and developmental lineage. Obligate OXPHOS eliminates highly mutated cells by apoptosis, whereas glycolytic conditions promote their competitive displacement. Individual loci exert modest but non-redundant effects that predict cell state beyond aggregate mutation burden, and cancer-recurrent variants are enriched among mutations linked to reduced mitochondrial transcription. Thus, mtDIVE links mtDNA genotypes to cellular phenotypes, separating the consequences of mutation identity from mutational load.

last_author.name: Sfeir, A.
last_author.affiliation: Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center

preprints.title: STEER-seq: a recombinase based platform for pooled multimodal single-cell perturbation screening
preprints.abstract: Pooled gain-of-function screening is a powerful method for screening for transcription factors whose overexpression leads to changes in cellular identity. However, variable transgene copy number, integration site and genomic context from random viral integration can confound quantitative comparisons between perturbations. We present STEER-seq (Single-cell Transgene Expression via Exchange Recombination sequencing), a virus-free platform for pooled ORF gain-of-function screening in human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs). STEER-seq combines irreversible Bxb1-mediated integration at a defined genomic safe-harbour locus with promoterless donor libraries and barcode-enabled perturbation tracking, enabling single-copy expression from a common promoter and genomic context and direct recovery of perturbation identity by single-cell sequencing. In a focused haematopoietic screen, SPI1 expression alone was sufficient to drive differentiation towards HSC/MPP-like progenitors in the absence of exogenous cytokines, with transient induction generating progenitors that retained multilineage haematopoietic differentiation potential. Joint RNA-chromatin accessibility profiling linked transcription factor-induced transcriptional responses to chromatin remodelling and enabled reconstruction of perturbation-induced gene regulatory networks, including a RUNX2-driven osteoblast programme. Scaling STEER-seq to around 2,000 human coding sequences enabled systematic discovery of transcription factors capable of inducing distinct cell-state programmes, including neural progenitor-, melanocyte- and vascular smooth muscle-like states, as well as maintenance of pluripotency. STEER-seq provides a scalable, quantitative framework for single-cell and multimodal gain-of-function screening, enabling functional discovery and engineering of human cell identity.

preprints.title: The CUP-SHAPED COTYLEDON 2 - MIR164A regulatory feedback loop directs leaf morphogenesis
preprints.abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) establish the spatio-temporal gene expression patterns necessary for reproducible development of organisms. MicroRNAs have emerged as important regulators of gene expression controlling either target gene levels, spatial patterns or timing. These molecular functions may vary depending on how they are integrated into GRNs. Here we used the Arabidopsis leaf as a model to study the genetic and molecular interactions between the CUP-SHAPED COTYLEDON 2 (CUC2) transcription factor and its negative regulator, miR164A. Quantitative morphometric analyses showed that miR164A acts from early stages during leaf development regulating CUC2 expression dynamic rather than the spatial distribution of CUC2. At the molecular level, CUC2 directly activates MIR164A expression, forming a single negative feedback loop. Further, using a ratiometric approach, we identified a cis-regulatory element (CRE) sufficient to drive CUC2-dependent MIR164A expression at the leaf sinus. Ordinary differential equation (ODE) modelling suggests that CUC2-CRE may control the timely accumulation of CUC2. Accordingly, quantification of CUC2 protein accumulation dynamics using a spatio-temporal mean cartography strategy in CRISPR cis-regulatory variants at the MIR164A locus revealed that CUC2-dependent MIRA164A expression is required to maintain both the precise timing of CUC2 expression and CUC2 levels. Altogether, our work provides experimental evidence for a specific role of the CUC2-MIR164A module in shaping leaf development, highlighting the contribution of network topology to GRN functions.

last_author.name: Arnaud, N.
last_author.affiliation: INRAE, Institut Jean-Pierre Bourgin (IJPB), INRAE-AgroParisTech INRA Centre de Versailles-Grignon

preprints.title: AI-Driven Design of Next-Generation Immunoinformatics Multi-Epitope Subunit Vaccine Targeting the Most Virulent Mpox Proteome: A Structural and Kinetic Validation Framework
preprints.abstract: The resurgence of the Mpox virus (MPXV) highlights the urgent need for scalable, mutation-resistant countermeasures. Slow development timelines hinder traditional empirical vaccine discovery, while conventional vaccinology often yields high false-positive rates because it relies on static, linear sequence-based screening. These classical informatics filters consistently fail to predict physical structural stability or the dynamic presentation of immune cells under physiological conditions, creating a distinct translational gap between computational design and in vitro efficacy. To address these limitations, here we engineered an advanced, AI-augmented vaccine discovery pipeline targeting the most virulent components of the MPXV proteome. We systematically screened eight critical viral targets essential for replication, membrane morphogenesis, and host-cell entry to map highly conserved T-cell and B-cell epitopes. Moving beyond standard heuristic filtering, we implemented a high-fidelity deep learning validation layer: ESM-2 protein language models (pLMs) were deployed to calculate pseudo-perplexity scores across chimeric linker junctions (EAAAK, GPGPG) to guarantee structural naturalness, MHCflurry ensemble models successfully verified active intracellular antigen presentation, and structure-informed graph neural networks (GNNs) simulated the physical node-attention dynamics of the immune synapse. Finally, recurrent neural networks (RNNs)-driven mRNA kinetic modeling optimized translation initiation rates and minimum free energy profiles during in silico cloning. This multi-layered pipeline successfully yielded three structurally refined, multi-epitope vaccine constructs optimized for maximum global population coverage. ESM-2 structural validation confirmed exceptionally low perplexity scores at structural junctions, indicating that the engineered chimaeras have native-like stability and a minimized risk of proteolysis. GNN-based immune synapse modeling demonstrated highly stable binding kinetics and robust binding free energies between the target epitopes and human HLA alleles. Furthermore, RNN kinetic optimizations established that the cDNA sequences are optimized for high-yield expression in heterologous expression hosts without risk of ribosomal stalling or translational bottlenecks. This study establishes a deep learning-augmented framework that bridges the gap between theoretical sequence optimization and biopharmaceutical scalability. By validating the structural naturalness, real-world immunogenicity, and manufacturing kinetics of our vaccine chimeras, this framework presents a robust, proactive paradigm for rapid vaccine architecture against emerging orthopoxvirus threats.
