preprints.title: Active maintenance of accessible chromatin at poised meiotic promoters by the NFYA-NURF axis is required for meiotic entry in mice
preprints.abstract: Developmental genes often acquire accessible chromatin prior to their activation, yet the mechanisms regulating this permissive state remain poorly understood. During spermatogenesis, many meiotic gene promoters display this poised state in spermatogonia, characterized by accessible promoters and paused RNA Pol II occupancy before their activation during meiosis. Here, we identify the NURF chromatin remodeling complex, comprised of SMARCA5 and its accessory subunit BPTF, as a key regulator of this process. We demonstrate that the transcription factor NFYA interacts with SMARCA5 and is required for its occupancy at poised meiotic gene promoters. Approximately one-third of poised meiotic gene promoters is co-occupied by NFYA, SMARCA5, and BPTF. Germline deletion of Smarca5 disrupts chromatin accessibility at poised meiotic promoters, impairs transcriptional program required for mitosis-to-meiosis transition, resulting in developmental arrest at meiotic entry. These findings identify NFYA-NURF as a key regulatory axis that regulates accessible chromatin at developmentally poised meiotic genes and primes them for activation later during meiosis.

last_author.name: Ozata, D. M.
last_author.affiliation: Stockholm University

preprints.title: CRISCross: Integration of Epigenetic Information for Deep-Learning-Based Prediction of CRISPR-Cas9 Off-Targets Across Cell Types
preprints.abstract: CRISPR-Cas9 enables precise genome editing but remains limited by off-target effects, raising safety concerns and necessitating accurate prediction. Although epigenetic features influence Cas9 binding and cleavage, their predictive signals are often weak, highlyvariable, and context-dependent, limiting the effectiveness of existing machine learning approaches. Cross-cell-type settings are especially challenging: epigenetic landscapes differ substantially, and models trained on one cell type frequently fail to generalize. Here, we systematically investigate the role of epigenetic context in off-target prediction and demonstrate that its utility depends on modeling interactions with sequence features rather than treating it as an independent signal. Tabular and deep learning experiments demonstrate that epigenetic features provide a consistent but modestly complementary signal, and that late-stage fusion strategies are insufficient to effectively exploit this information. To address this, we introduce CRISCross, a cross-attention-based architecture that captures sequence-epigenetic interactions at the nucleotide level, alongside CRISPRAT, a synthetic pretraining strategy that learns transferable representations from genome-derived sgRNA-off-target pairs without relying on dataset-specific pretraining. CRISCross, incorporating AlphaGenome-derived chromatin accessibility signals, shows better predictive performance than sequence-only baselines across three independent test datasets spanning two cell types, demonstrating improved generalization across guide RNAs, datasets, and cellular contexts. This is particularly relevant for therapeutic applications involving cell types or patient-derived contexts that lack dedicated experimental datasets. In such settings, predicted chromatin accessibility may provide scalable contextual information when direct epigenomic profiling is unavailable or impractical. Together, these results show that accurate CRISPR off-target prediction benefits from interaction-aware integration of epigenetic context alongside generalizable pretraining strategies.

preprints.title: Continuous Large Maf Activity Maintains Fast Myofiber Identity and Multicellular Homeostasis in Adult Skeletal Muscle
preprints.abstract: Fast myofibers are preferentially affected during aging, exhibiting atrophy and shifts toward slower myofiber programs, yet the mechanisms preserving established fast-fiber identity remain unclear. Here, we show that the large Maf transcription factors Mafa, Mafb, and Maf are continuously required to maintain type IIb myofiber identity in adult skeletal muscle. Inducible deletion of large Mafs caused near-complete loss of type IIb fibers, a transition toward type IIx/IIa states, reduced strength, and increased fatigue resistance. RNA-seq and ATAC-seq revealed transcriptional and chromatin accessibility remodeling across the fast myosin locus, characterized by persistent loss of Myh4 expression and increased accessibility around Myh1. Single-nucleus RNA-seq identified transient myonuclei co-expressing multiple myosin isoforms before emergence of a Myh1-dominant state, accompanied by remodeling of non-myonuclear cell populations. These changes shared features with aging- and denervation-associated muscle remodeling. Thus, continuous large Maf activity maintains adult fast myofiber identity and coordinates skeletal muscle tissue homeostasis.

last_author.name: Fujita, R.
last_author.affiliation: University of Tsukuba

preprints.title: Cross Study Regulator Activity Analysis Reveals Convergent Programs in alpha Synuclein PFF Models of Parkinson Disease
preprints.abstract: Alpha-synuclein preformed fibril (PFF) models reproduce features of Parkinson disease (PD), but differences in brain region, cell composition, and experimental design complicate comparisons across studies. We reconstructed study-specific regulatory networks using ARACNe (Algorithm for the Reconstruction of Accurate Cellular Networks) and inferred transcription factor (TF) and transcription cofactor activity using VIPER (Virtual Inference of Protein-activity by Enriched Regulon analysis). Five transcriptomic comparisons from four mouse PFF datasets were analyzed, with human PD single-nucleus RNA-sequencing data used to assess cross-species agreement. In the dopamine-neuron-enriched dataset GSE252967, PFF exposure was associated with increased activity of stress- and inflammation-related TFs, including JUND and RELA, and decreased activity of dopaminergic-identity regulators, including NR4A2, LMX1B, FOXA1, FOXA2, PITX3, and EN1. Several regulators were connected to Th in the inferred network. The substantia nigra bulk dataset GSE296779 showed reduced activity of ATF4- and XBP1-associated protein homeostasis and unfolded protein response programs, supported by regulon-weighted gene-set enrichment. Supporting mouse comparisons showed limited overlap in individual TFs but identified changes in inflammatory, glial, and stress-related programs. Agreement between inferred activity and transcript-level changes ranged from 64% to 100% in these comparisons. Human PD data showed cell-type-dependent agreement with mouse findings. EN1 and PITX3 were shared between the mouse and human networks upstream of Th/TH and showed reduced inferred activity in all seven human cell types, alongside nonsignificant decreases in the mouse dataset. These analyses identified changes in dopaminergic-identity, protein homeostasis, and inflammatory transcriptional programs across mouse PFF models, with partial support in human PD.
preprints.corresponding_institution: University of Tennessee Health Science Center

preprints.title: Developmental rewiring of EHMT1 function during human cortical neurogenesis
preprints.abstract: Ubiquitously expressed chromatin regulators orchestrate cell-type-specific gene expression programs, yet how they acquire distinct regulatory functions during development remains fundamentally unresolved. Using temporally controlled protein depletion during human cortical neurogenesis in vitro, we show that the autism-associated histone methyltransferase EHMT1 is developmentally repurposed from epiblast to cortical neurons. Broadly expressed zinc finger proteins recruit EHMT1 to distinct cis-regulatory elements within changing chromatin landscapes associated with lineage-specific transcription factor activity, with extensive remodeling of EHMT1 enhancer occupancy during neural induction dependent on ZNF462. This genomic rewiring is accompanied by a fundamental shift from restraining premature developmental gene expression in pluripotent cells to supporting neuronal programs, with distinct transcriptional consequences of EHMT1 loss across neural progenitors and excitatory and inhibitory neuronal subtypes. Timed depletion and recovery experiments identify the neural progenitor stage as the onset of a developmental period during which EHMT1 is required for faithful neuronal maturation. Remarkably, EHMT1 can re-engage stage-specific targets after prolonged deficiency, allowing extensive transcriptional recovery with only limited molecular scarring. These findings reveal how ubiquitous epigenetic machinery acquires developmental specificity while demonstrating the resilience of developmental gene regulatory programs to prolonged disruption, with implications for neurodevelopmental disorders.

last_author.name: Stadtfeld, M.
last_author.affiliation: Weill Cornell Medicine

preprints.title: Functional diversification of ERF transcription factors in land plants
preprints.abstract: The ERF family is one of the largest families of plant-specific transcription factors, controlling diverse developmental processes and stress responses. Extensive gene duplication and redundancy in flowering plants have generated large ERF repertoires, complicating comparisons of ERF function across land-plant lineages. How ERF transcription factor repertoires and their functions have evolved across land plants remains poorly understood. Here, we reconstruct the phylogenetic relationships and expansion of ERF transcription factors across land plants and exploit the compact ERF repertoire of the model liverwort Marchantia polymorpha to investigate their functional diversification. Systematic gain-of-function analysis reveals that different clades of ERFs can drive distinct cell fate and reprogramming outcomes in Marchantia, in addition to stress-related functions. Interestingly, we found that MpERF2, the sole Group I ERF in Marchantia, phylogenetically related to the WIND clade, promotes rhizoid cell differentiation. This contrast with the role of the WIND clade in wound-induced regeneration in Arabidopsis. Heterologous expression of AtWIND1 in Marchantia was also capable of inducing rhizoid formation, supporting the hypothesis that this reprogramming capacity is conserved at the protein level. On the other hand, loss of MpERF2 reduced rhizoid coverage but did not significantly impair regeneration. These findings provide an evolutionary framework for understanding the functional evolution of ERF transcription factors and how conserved transcriptional regulators are co-opted into novel developmental programs during the radiation of land plants.

last_author.name: Romani, F.
last_author.affiliation: Department of Plant Sciences, University of Cambridge

preprints.corresponding_institution: Department of Plant Sciences, University of Cambridge

preprints.title: Genetic circuit rewiring underlies a lineage-specific patterning machinery on butterfly wings
preprints.abstract: Phenotypes evolve through changes in gene regulatory networks (GRNs), but how changes in network topology contribute to phenotypic evolution is still poorly understood. Butterfly wing color patterns provide a tractable system to answer this question. Here, we compared the expression of four color pattern genes, WntA, pdm3, ivory, and Optix, in five nymphalid butterflies, and tested their regulatory connections through genetic perturbations in three species spanning 80 million years of divergence. We found broadly conserved 1) regulatory hierarchy linking early pattern instruction via WntA signaling to subsequent color readout via ivory and Optix, 2) positive autoregulation in WntA signaling, and 3) positive regulation from WntA signaling to pdm3. Notably, we discovered lineage-specific negative feedback from pdm3 to WntA signaling in Vanessa cardui, which closes a reciprocal WntA-pdm3 feedback loop that refines complex pattern elements. We show that developmental programs can evolve by rewiring internal interactions among pre-existing GRN nodes, emphasizing the importance of network topology in phenotypic evolution.

last_author.name: Mazo-Vargas, A.
last_author.affiliation: Duke University

preprints.title: Genome-scale mapping of plant transcription factor effector domains reveals conserved regulatory principles across eukaryotes
preprints.abstract: Eukaryotic life spans species that diverged over a billion years ago, yet our molecular view of gene regulation remains heavily skewed toward Opisthokonta model systems, particularly yeast and humans. The degree to which the protein features governing transcriptional regulation are conserved across eukaryotes or have diversified within individual eukaryotic supergroups remains unresolved. To provide a distinct evolutionary reference point, we used a massively parallel reporter assay in plant cells to identify transcriptional effector domains and define their sequence constraints, measuring ~26,000 protein fragments tiling nearly all Arabidopsis transcription factors (1,859 proteins). Comparison with the activity of the same peptide sequences in yeast revealed that activation is governed by a mixture of deeply conserved biochemical features and lineage-dependent functional differences across widely divergent eukaryotic lineages. Likewise, plant repression domains are governed by flexible sequence grammars that extend beyond conserved repression motifs. Together, these results reveal both broadly conserved and clade-specific principles governing eukaryotic transcriptional regulation.

last_author.name: Shih, P. M.
last_author.affiliation: University of California, Berkeley

preprints.title: Probing Genomic Foundation Models with Splice-Variant Perturbations
preprints.abstract: As benchmarks saturate, traditional validation methods fail to capture the probabilistic representations of genomic foundation models. This study probes self-supervised generalists (NTv3 650M, Evo2 40B, Genos 10B) alongside task-specific specialists (SpliceAI, AlphaGenome, Borzoi) using a mechanistically focused paradigm centered on expert-curated single-nucleotide substitutions within the splicing regions of the exon-rich OPA1 gene. Extending this analysis across the broader corpus of OPA1 mutations, variants of uncertain significance (VUS), and an independent 65-gene dataset of spliceogenic mutations demonstrates that generalists can match task-specific networks. Training data scale, genetic diversity, and evolutionary context are key for capturing RNA splicing syntax, whereas sparse routing may constrain performance. Mechanistically, foundation models exhibit a compute-asymmetry: the Evo2 40B model frontloads compute into massive parameter scale to resolve single-nucleotide variants within a narrow 425-bp context window, whereas the bidirectional NTv3 650M model and the Genos 10B mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture backload compute to inference, requiring spatial logit aggregation and expansive context windows of up to 94 kb. Furthermore, classification accuracy across these foundation models benefitted from locus-specific thresholding rather than mutation-class calibration, exposing representation boundaries of the models.

last_author.name: Alavi, M. V.
last_author.affiliation: 712 North Inc.

preprints.title: Spatially resolved tumor-microenvironment architecture defines therapeutic response in unresectable hepatoblastoma
preprints.abstract: Background: Hepatoblastoma exhibits variable therapeutic response that is not fully explained by current risk stratification. While prior studies have characterized tumor composition, the role of spatial organization in determining outcome, particularly in unresectable disease requiring transplantation under immunosuppression, remains unclear. Methods: We integrated spatial transcriptomics using the 10x Genomics Visium platform (n = 11 tumors) with single-cell spatial molecular imaging using NanoString CosMx (n = 3 tumors) on post-chemotherapy explant specimens across clinically defined groups (relapse-prone unresectable, non-relapse unresectable, and resectable hepatoblastoma). Spatial deconvolution, module scoring, spatial co-localization, and cell-cell interaction analyses were used to define region-level transcriptional programs and their underlying cellular organization. Results: We identified three spatial architectures associated with clinical outcome. Relapse-prone tumors exhibited a centralized, TME-dominated organization enriched for progenitor-like, cycling, and stress-responsive tumor cell states co-localized with SPP1+ TAMs and CAFs, with enrichment of hypoxia response, extracellular matrix remodeling, and Midkine (MDK-LRP1) signaling. Non-relapse tumors displayed a distributed architecture with compartmentalized tumor-immune interactions, increased immune engagement, and preserved epithelial differentiation, including inflammatory hepatocyte-like states. Resection samples showed reduced tumor cell state heterogeneity and more uniform TME-immune organization. Conclusions: Integration of regional and single-cell spatial transcriptomics across two platforms reveals that the chemo-remodeled tumor architecture of hepatoblastoma encodes spatially organized tumor cell-TME interactions as central determinants of therapeutic response.

last_author.name: Sindhi, R.
last_author.affiliation: UPMC Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh

preprints.title: Spatiotemporal Mapping of Glomerular Endothelial Regeneration Identifies Apold1 as an Intrinsic Regulator of Repair
preprints.abstract: Abstract Endothelial cell (EC) injury is central to the pathogenesis of various renal disorders, highlighting the critical importance of vascular repair for restoring organ health. However, due to limited access to human tissue during active regeneration, the exact reparative processes remain largely unknown. This study aimed to investigate regeneration mechanisms specifically within the glomerular microvasculature by utilizing a selective endothelial cell injury (ECI) model in mice.Lineage tracing identified the origin of regenerating ECs. To uncover the transcriptional dynamics driving these reparative changes, we combined single-cell RNA sequencing and Xenium spatial transcriptomics (ST), mapping distinct glomerular EC (gEC) subpopulations across different phases of injury and recovery. Apold1 emerged as a key regulatory candidate within this process. To functionally validate this gene's specific role during the regenerative phase, Apold1-deficient (Apold1-/-) mice underwent the ECI model. After showing that gECs regenerate primarily from local, pre-existing renal ECs, our transcriptomic analysis identified 10 distinct gEC subpopulations and revealed a complex temporal pattern of regeneration. This process begins with the expression of genes associated with inflammation, followed sequentially by endothelial cell (EC) migration, the activation of immediate early genes, vascular remodeling and cellular proliferation. Within this dynamic process, the EC-specific gene Apold1 was identified as a key regulatory candidate. Apold1-/- mice exhibited impaired endothelial regeneration, characterized by increased endothelial activation and greater immune cell infiltration seven days post-ECI. To our knowledge, this is the first study to elucidate the spatiotemporal mechanisms of glomerular endothelial cell regeneration. By identifying local gECs as the primary source of repair, and stablishing the change in their expression pattern during regeneration, as well as identifying Apold1 as an intrinsic regulator, we have laid the groundwork for future research on renal microvascular disorders.

last_author.name: Sradnick, J.

preprints.title: The Human Gut Cell Atlas v1.0: A Unified, Community-BuiltReference of Cellular Diversity Across the Gut
preprints.abstract: Single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) studies have transformed our understanding of cellular diversity in the human intestine, but differences in anatomical sampling, experimental processing and cell-type nomenclature limit comparison across datasets. Here, we present the Human Gut Cell Atlas (HGCA) V1, a community-curated reference of 944,390 healthy and disease-adjacent intestinal cells from 502 samples, 265 donors and 24 landmark studies, linked to detailed anatomical, clinical, and technical metadata. As this metadata is of critical importance to human biology, we developed MetaManager, an open source data management framework for standardized metadata collection and tracking. A five-level consensus taxonomy resolves 94 homeostatic cell identities and enables transferrable, high-resolution annotation of new gut datasets. By assembling cell identity, sampling metadata, and independent spatial validation, intestinal segment and radial tissue depth were revealed to systematically shape cellular composition and transcriptional state, enabling inference of the presence of sampling-dependent tissue niches, including lymphoid follicles. Reference mapping accurately and rapidly recovered cohort-level Crohn's disease and treatment signatures without de novo annotation, while mapping human intestinal organoids quantified cell-type-specific identity, regional specification, maturation, and transcriptional fidelity to native tissue. The HGCA V1 provides a standardized cellular, anatomical coordinate, and metadata system for reproducible, high-quality analysis of intestinal biology across healthy tissue, disease-associated remodelling, and experimental models, providing a continuously evolving community reference for cumulative discovery in human intestinal biology.
preprints.corresponding_institution: Division of Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition, Boston Children's Hospital, Boston, MA, USA

preprints.title: A foundation model for brain organoid network dynamics uncovers intrinsic computation and convergent disease phenotypes
preprints.abstract: Brain organoids develop self-organizing neural networks that can be used to model neurodevelopment and disease. Here we introduce PULSE, a foundation model developed using over 900 hours of high-density microelectrode array recordings of in vitro and ex vivo neural tissue. We show that this single model can address two open questions: how disease-associated variants alter network development, and how naive circuits encode information. PULSE revealed accelerated network maturation in held-out human 16p11.2-deletion organoids. It also revealed a change in network coordination shared with SHANK3 deficiency. Because organoids develop without sensory input, they let us ask how circuits encode information before any representation is learned. Closed-loop control of a virtual inverted pendulum engaged existing spontaneous activity patterns rather than creating new ones. PULSE provides a common reference frame for neural circuits across genotypes, protocols and tasks.

last_author.name: Mostajo-Radji, M. A.
last_author.affiliation: University of California Santa Cruz

preprints.title: A perturbation atlas of mouse neural organoids resolves macroglial reactivity and nominates drivers of degeneration
preprints.abstract: Understanding neuro-glial roles in homeostasis and disease requires scalable central nervous system (CNS) models, particularly as macroglia like astrocytes and Muller glia remain challenging to study in slow-developing human systems. Here, we generate and map the cellular diversity of mouse neural organoids spanning multiple brain regions and the retina. Benchmarking transcriptomic maturation against in vivo references captures postnatal neuro-macroglial states within a month. We show that macroglia are highly responsive to inflammatory cues and adopt specific transcriptomic states also found in vivo. Through a single-cell perturbation screen targeting 13 Muller-glia-specific pathways, we map how certain inflammatory cytokines drive degeneration-like stress programs in photoreceptors and distinct reactive states in Muller glia, including an Oncostatin M-driven chaperone-associated state. Mechanistically, we identify gp130-STAT3 signaling as a targetable driver of macroglial reactivity and photoreceptor distress. Together, these single-cell atlases provide a foundation for dissecting cellular crosstalk and neuro-glial pathology in the mature CNS.

last_author.name: Camp, J. G.
last_author.affiliation: Roche Institute of Human Biology (IHB)

preprints.title: An integrated multi-omic atlas of the choroid plexus highlights conserved molecular programs of epithelial function
preprints.abstract: The choroid plexus (ChP) is a specialized epithelial tissue responsible for production of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), maintenance of the blood-CSF barrier and regulation of CSF-borne signaling factors. However, despite the ChP's central role in CSF homeostasis, conserved molecular programs of ChP epithelial function across species and conditions remain incompletely defined. In this study, we integrated eight mouse and human single-cell/nucleus RNA-seq datasets to build a multi-species ChP atlas capturing major epithelial, stromal, vascular, and immune populations. Cross-dataset differential expression identified a conserved epithelial gene program encompassing ion transport, barrier function, ciliogenesis, and secretory signaling, while prioritizing understudied genes including CLIC6 and VAT1L. Co-expression network analysis resolved conserved epithelial meta-programs, and transcription factor regulatory inference identified OTX2, MSX1, and GLIS3 among conserved regulators of epithelial gene expression. We also generated a novel Visium HD spatial transcriptomic atlas of mouse fourth-ventricle ChP to orthogonally validate epithelial modules. Lastly, cross-tissue analyses revealed substantial transcriptional overlap between ChP and retinal pigment epithelium, including shared epithelial genes and OTX2-associated regulatory relationships. Together, these findings define conserved molecular programs of ChP epithelial specialization, nominate candidate regulators for functional investigation, and provide an integrated cross-species and spatial resource for studying ChP physiology.

last_author.name: Kahle, K. T.
last_author.affiliation: Massachusetts General Hospital

preprints.title: Bayesian phylogenetics with incomplete lineage tracing data
preprints.abstract: Single-cell lineage tracing is rapidly emerging as a powerful method to track the dynamics of cell populations through time. Specifically, CRISPR-Cas9-based dynamic lineage tracing methods generate high-resolution data with the potential to investigate increasingly complex biological processes. However, single-cell readouts are inherently lossy, resulting in significant sparsity in lineage barcode alignments. Here, we present a mechanistic model of barcode loss implemented in the Bayesian framework BEAST 2, enabling phylogenetic inference from sparse datasets without the need for data filtering. Through simulations, we find that incorporating a mechanistic model of loss improves accuracy across all estimates in phylogenetic analyses by enabling previously unusable data to contribute to the inference. We further demonstrate the model's utility across two datasets: one from a monoclonal cell culture and another from murine gastruloids. Consistent with our simulation findings, applying our model to these datasets recovers higher growth rates than workflows relying on standard data filtering, confirming that such filtering can lead to an underestimation of population expansion. Crucially, we demonstrate that our framework enables inference even from datasets whose sparsity previously prevented analysis, providing a robust foundation for extracting biological insights from lineage tracing experiments.

preprints.title: Cause-excluded Effect Evaluation: a framework for the faithful assessment of genetic perturbation target identification
preprints.abstract: Identifying which gene drives a desired cell-state transition is a foundational inverse problem in target discovery and cell-state engineering, yet far less developed than forward prediction. We show that prevailing benchmarks inflate performance through two artefacts: training leakage, where test-perturbation cells are seen during fitting, and evaluation leakage, where the perturbed gene's own expression change exposes the answer. Here, we introduce Cause-excluded Effect Evaluation (CEE), a framework that separates train and test perturbation targets, removes target-gene self-effects from expression profiles and scores candidates in downstream response space. With CEE, we find that simple structure-based methods consistently outperform complex deep learning models across 16 single-cell perturbation datasets, revealing that the recoverable signal is governed by low-rank and additive structure in perturbation responses rather than by model complexity. Our work disentangles evaluation artefacts from genuine predictive capacity and offers a design principle for developing perturbation target identification methods.

preprints.title: DECONVersation: Single Cell Foundation Model-Derived Embeddings for Robust Cell Type Deconvolution of Bulk RNA-seq
preprints.abstract: AI and deep learning have transformed single-cell transcriptomics, empowering unsupervised annotation, trajectory inference, and cross-dataset integration at scale. Here, we propose bulk RNA-seq deconvolution as a novel task for single-cell foundation models. Deconvolution estimates cell type proportions from bulk RNA-seq using single-cell reference data, with applications spanning tumor microenvironment profiling to the detection of disease-associated shifts in tissue composition. However, existing methods remain vulnerable to batch effects, subject-level variation, and marker gene selection sensitivity. We introduce DECONVersation, which leverages embeddings from pretrained and fine-tuned single-cell foundation models, coupled with a non-negative least squares solver, to estimate cell type proportions. Foundation model embeddings are robust to batch effects and implicitly encode complex gene relationships, sidestepping explicit marker gene selection. Benchmarked against MuSiC, DWLS, and BayesPrism, DECONVersation achieved comparable or superior performance across diverse tissues. Performance further improved with tissue-specific fine-tuning.

last_author.name: Fu, R.
last_author.affiliation: New York Genome Center

preprints.title: Deciphering auditory neuroprogenitor stemness for large-scale neuronal screening
preprints.abstract: Sensorineural hearing loss can arise from damage to sensory hair cells, auditory neurons or their synaptic connections, with auditory neuropathy and cochlear synaptopathy highlighting the importance of neural integrity for hearing. The mammalian cochlea has limited capacity to regenerate lost auditory neurons. Understanding the molecular programs that sustain cochlear progenitor expansion and neurogenic competence could support neuronal regeneration and provide renewable models for auditory drug discovery. We previously established that WNT activation combined with dual SMAD inhibition (CHIR-DS) supports scalable expansion and neuronal differentiation of mouse auditory neuroprogenitors (ANPGs). Here, we characterize the transcriptional, chromatin and metabolic changes associated with the induced state. RNA-seq and ATAC-seq identified reduced Id1 and Id2 expression and increased accessibility at proneural basic helix-loop-helix motifs, alongside transcriptional enrichment of translation, mTOR and glucose-metabolism programs. Compared with growth-factor controls, CHIR-DS-treated ANPGs showed slight increase in glycolysis at early passage. However, after long-term expansion, both glycolysis and mitochondrial respiration were markedly enhanced. Human fetal ANPGs also responded to CHIR-DS with increased sphere growth and retained neural differentiation capacity, providing proof of concept beyond the mouse system. Finally, neurons derived from stemness-induced ANPGs (siANs) supported a 384-well reporter assay and a 2,560-compound pilot screen that nominated candidate neurite-outgrowth enhancers. Together, these findings validate the pathway basis of ANPG stemness induction, characterize the resulting molecular and metabolic state, and demonstrate human feasibility and a neuronal screening application.

preprints.title: Engineered regulatory states resolve context-dependent genetics in macular degeneration
preprints.abstract: The effects of many genes and disease-associated variants remain hidden in standard cellular models, limiting functional interpretation. Here we engineer regulatory states via CRISPR activation of transcription factors (TFs) in human RPE-1 cells, a model for age-related macular degeneration (AMD). Multiome Perturb-seq profiling of single-TF perturbations identified regulators that selectively opened chromatin at AMD GWAS variants inaccessible in resting RPE-1. Priming of partner motifs in chromatin made accessible by single-TF perturbations predicted TF pairs generating emergent transcriptional states in combinatorial Perturb-seq, providing a design principle for selecting informative interactions. Distinct TF pairs also showed variable convergence between polygenic AMD signals and Mendelian retinal disease genes, supporting an omnigenic model shaped by regulatory states. Finally, Mosaic, a chromatin-informed model of TF interaction phenotypes, nominated out-of-sample regulators, including a higher-order combination with experimentally validated emergent effects on AMD-associated programs. Engineered regulatory states thus bring hidden disease biology within experimental reach.

preprints.title: Human Choroid Plexus Organoids Progress to Postnatal-like Maturation and Reveal a Closing Window of Developmental Plasticity
preprints.abstract: The choroid plexus (ChP) produces cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and forms the blood-CSF barrier, yet the developmental programme driving its maturation in humans remains poorly understood. Using a 15-timepoint single-cell RNA sequencing atlas of human ChP organoids benchmarked against human tissue, we resolve an ordered differentiation process comprising cell cycle exit, ciliogenesis and ion transporter expression. Maturation culminates in a transcriptional state with features of human adult ChP, establishing the first in vitro ChP model to reach postnatal-like milestones. Centrosome proteomics identified previously uncharacterised, stage-specific regulators of ciliogenesis. To probe developmental plasticity, we perturbed ChP organoids with valproic acid (VPA), a clinically used antiepileptic and established teratogen. Early VPA-mediated disruption of multiciliogenesis and secretion recovered upon drug withdrawal, whereas late treatment washout resulted in persistent impairment of mature transporters. Together, these findings resolve the developmental programme by which the ChP reaches functionally mature identity and identify a stage-dependent plasticity window during its maturation.

last_author.name: Pellegrini, L.
last_author.affiliation: King's College London

preprints.title: Intrinsically disordered regions influence protein motif usage in Drosophila Ubx and AbdA Hox proteins
preprints.abstract: Hox proteins are evolutionary conserved transcription factors guiding morphogenesis in all bilaterian animals. Conservation mainly concerns the homeodomain (HD), a helix-turn-helix DNA binding motif and flanking sequences close by. Besides, sequences are poorly conserved and disordered. Here we investigate how poorly conserved Intrinsically Disordered Regions (IDRs) influence Hox protein activity, focusing on a closely related Drosophila Hox pair and using a wide range of in vivo function. Studying Drosophila Ultrabithorax (Ubx) and AbdominalA (AbdA) proteins, we find that conserved protein motifs close to the HD are differently used in Ubx and AbdA. Coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations identify a large set of intra-molecular interactions, notably involving poorly conserved disordered regions upstream and downstream the HD. Swapping these regions in Ubx and AbdA alters protein functions and switches motif dependency in some biological situations. This suggests that IDRs, predicted to mediate large and dynamic sets of intramolecular interactions, influence protein motif usage in a context dependent manner.

preprints.title: Ligand-specific endothelial Notch signaling coordinates brain pericyte specification and expansion
preprints.abstract: Pericyte specification and expansion must be coordinated with vascular growth to establish a functional cerebrovascular network, yet how endothelial signals control these distinct developmental transitions remains incompletely understood. Here, using genetic manipulation, single-cell transcriptomic analysis, and longitudinal in vivo imaging in zebrafish, we identify ligand-specific endothelial Notch signaling as a mechanism coordinating brain pericyte development. Endothelial Jag2b is required for efficient pericyte specification from pericerebral progenitor pools and subsequently promotes Notch-dependent pericyte proliferation and population expansion. By contrast, endothelial Dll4 restrains pericyte proliferation and functionally opposes Jag2b-dependent expansion, demonstrating that distinct endothelial Notch ligands generate different developmental outputs. Endothelial Notch activation increases jag2b expression, and genetic interaction analyses establish Jag2b as an important mediator of Notch-dependent pericyte expansion. Moreover, genetic disruption of piezo1 reduces brain pericyte abundance, whereas endothelial jag2b expression rescues this phenotype, placing Jag2b downstream of Piezo1-dependent hemodynamic signaling. Together, these findings reveal a ligand-specific endothelial Notch program that integrates hemodynamic cues with endothelial-pericyte communication to coordinate the specification and expansion of brain pericytes during cerebrovascular development.

preprints.title: Multi-Omic and Spatial Profiling Defines Outcome-Associated Tumor States in Head and Neck Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma
preprints.abstract: Abstract Head and neck adenoid cystic carcinoma (HNACC) shows highly variable clinical behavior that histopathological features only partly predict, and prognostic biomarkers for aggressive disease at diagnosis remain limited. Here, we show by integrating bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomes from 25 HNACC tumors that poor survival is marked by profound loss of myoepithelial tumor cells and expansion of luminal tumor states. Both outcome groups share a myoepithelial-like origin, but aggressive tumors converge on an actively dividing, MYC/E2F-driven luminal state concentrated in discrete spatial niches. Aggressiveness therefore reflects where tumors end along a shared developmental path rather than a distinct lineage or altered immune infiltration. A four-gene classifier capturing this state predicted survival in an independent cohort, outperforming larger signatures and flagging aggressive subgroups in two others. These findings define a lineage proliferation axis linked to HNACC outcome, providing a basis for prospective risk stratification and proliferative-directed therapy.

last_author.affiliation: University of New Mexico

preprints.title: Outgrowth of Mouse Sensory Neurons is not Mediated by Regeneration Associated Genes in Early Postnatal Stages
preprints.abstract: Peripheral neurons exhibit robust regeneration after nerve injury in adulthood; a process linked to the activation of regeneration-associated genes (RAGs). However, the mechanisms underlying nerve regeneration during early postnatal development remain poorly understood. In a previous work, we observed that motoneurons axotomized at early postnatal stages regenerate without overexpressing RAGs, contrasting with the expected RAG activation observed in postnatal day 30 (P30) mice. To determine whether this phenomenon extends to sensory neurones, we investigated two paradigmatic dorsal root ganglia populations: proprioceptive (PV) and nociceptive (TrpV1) neurones, which exhibit distinct regenerative capacities in adult mice. Following sciatic nerve crush injury at P4, P10, and P30, both neuronal subtypes demonstrated robust axonal regeneration across all postnatal stages, with nociceptors exhibiting significantly superior regeneration compared to proprioceptors. Remarkably, no substantial neuronal death was observed at any developmental timepoint. However, RNA sequencing revealed that P4 and P10 sensory neurones failed to upregulate RAGs following injury, whereas P30 neurones exhibited the expected pro-regenerative transcriptional programme. Pathway enrichment analysis confirmed that classical regeneration-associated signalling pathways were activated exclusively in young adults, whilst developmental and inflammatory pathways predominated in early postnatal stages. Using the conditioning lesion paradigm in primary dorsal root ganglia cultures, we demonstrated that only P30 neurones exhibited enhanced neurite outgrowth following conditioning lesion, whilst P4 and P10 neurones showed no conditioning effect or reduced outgrowth, respectively. These findings indicate that early postnatal sensory neurones possess intrinsic growth capacity independent of RAG activation, suggesting fundamentally distinct regenerative mechanisms across developmental stages.

preprints.title: PRC2-binding regions are hotspots of DNA methylation entropy in pre-cancer and cancer
preprints.abstract: DNA methylation aberrations and variability are pervasive features of cancer, yet their relationship with chromatin regulation remains incompletely understood. Across hundreds of matched tumor-normal methylomes, regions with the highest methylation entropy in both tumor and normal tissues were consistently enriched for PRC2-associated factors. In tumors, inter-sample methylation variability was increased across the full range of PRC2-associated levels, while mean methylation progressively increased from low- to high-PRC2-binding regions; this gradient was substantially weaker in matched normal tissues. PRC2-associated regions with higher DNA methylation levels were preferentially associated with poised and repressed chromatin states, reduced chromatin accessibility, and reduced gene expression. Independent normal-precancer-cancer cohorts showed that this PRC2-associated methylation state emerges early, with precancerous and malignant tissues displaying highly similar profiles that are distinct from those of healthy tissues. Single-cell colon cancer methylomes independently confirmed increased methylation entropy at PRC2 regions. Higher PRC2-region entropy was associated with scores reflecting hypoxic states, aggressive tumor features, and poorer survival outcomes. Collectively, these findings identify PRC2-binding regions as hotspots of DNA methylation variability that become dysregulated during tumorigenesis.

preprints.title: Repeated malaria exposure reprograms Vδ2+ γδT cell chromatin accessibility and immune function toward a reversible hyporesponsive state
preprints.abstract: V{delta}2+ {gamma}{delta} T cells contribute to antimalarial immunity via pro-inflammatory and cytotoxic mechanisms. Among children who have experienced repeated episodes of malaria, V{delta}2+ T cells develop reduced pro-inflammatory function through mechanisms that remain unknown. We hypothesized that recurrent malaria drives coordinated epigenetic and transcriptional remodeling of these semi-innate cells. Using PBMC from Ugandan children in cohorts spanning high and low transmission (10 children) and longitudinally across a marked decline in transmission (20 children, 3 timepoints), we profiled the epigenome and transcriptome of V{delta}2+ T cells by paired bulk ATAC-seq and RNA-seq and by CITE-seq. Higher malaria exposure was associated with reduced V{delta}2+ T cell TNF and IFN{gamma} production and with thousands of differentially accessible chromatin regions. Immunoregulatory genes including LYN, PLCG2, and HAVCR2 (Tim-3) showed increased chromatin accessibility and/or expression at high exposure, whereas pro-inflammatory gene (IFNG, GZMK, IL7R) and AP-1 (JUN/FOS) motif accessibility were increased at low exposure; linkage of regulatory elements with target genes corroborated these associations. Single-cell transcriptional analysis identified a cytotoxic CD8+CD16+CD57+ V{delta}2+ T cell subset. In our in vitro model, repeated stimulation with malaria-infected red blood cells or the phosphoantigen HMBPP was similarly associated with reduced V{delta}2+ T cell degranulation and cytokine production. Diminished responsiveness was predominantly TCR-dependent, accompanied by heightened p38 signaling, and was partially reversed by rest induced by the tyrosine kinase inhibitor dasatinib. Together these data reveal how repeated malaria may reshape cellular immunity by reprogramming V{delta}2+ T cells toward a reversible, hyporesponsive state and highlight targets for therapeutically restoring their function.

last_author.name: Jagannathan, P.
last_author.affiliation: Stanford University

preprints.title: Robust V(D)J Recombination in the Absence of SA1/2-mediated Chromatin Loops
preprints.abstract: The cohesin ring complex organizes and mediates functional activity of the genome through chromatin loop extrusion1,2. Cohesin comprises a core SMC1-SMC3-RAD21 ring associated with multiple regulatory proteins, including SA1 and SA2 paralogs that bind mutually-exclusively to a RAD21 site3,4. Functional studies of cohesin complexes in vivo often employ inactivation of particular components2,3. However, inactivation of SA1 or SA2 in mice is limited by mouse embryonic lethality5-7 and, for dual SA1/2-inactivation by cycling cell lethality8-10. For these reasons, it remains unknown whether the requirement for SA1/2 in loop extrusion in vitro11,12 applies in vivo1,2, and whether these factors have overlapping or distinct functions in regulating this process3. Here, we employ G0/G1-arrested v-Abl pro-B lines, which are viable in the absence of cohesin-complex factors13,14, to dissect SA1 and SA2 functions in V(D)J recombination, a strictly G0/G1-specific process that harnesses loop extrusion to effect distinct Igh and Ig{kappa} locus recombination mechanisms15,16. Robust long-range Igh or Ig{kappa} V(D)J recombination continued unabated in the absence of SA1 or SA2. However, inactivation of both abrogated most positioned chromatin loops genome-wide and also abolished long-range Igh V(D)J recombination with a phenotype similar to RAD21 (cohesin) inactivation13. Yet, robust Ig{kappa} V(D)J recombination continued upon dual SA1/2-inactivation, which along with Hi-C findings, demonstrates ongoing loop-extrusion in the absence of SA1/2. Correspondingly, replacement of weak Igh V(D)J recombination signal sequences (RSSs) that target V(D)J recombination activity, with strong Ig{kappa} counterparts15 restored long-range Igh V(D)J recombination in SA1/2 inactivated cells. We conclude that SA1/2 together maintain loop extrusion impediments and genome-wide architecture in G0/G1-arrested cells; and, in their absence, loop extrusion proceeds unimpeded. Remarkably, strong RSSs allow Ig{kappa} to function normally in the absence of internal positioned loop structure across the 3.1-mega-base Ig{kappa} locus. We discuss implications of our findings for long-range gene regulation in G0/G1-arrested cells more broadly.

preprints.title: Single Cell Proteomics reveals partial uncoupling of the Glycerol-3-Phosphate shuttle to compensate for Electron Transport Chain dysfunction in Alexander Disease GFAP mutations
preprints.abstract: Alexander disease (AxD) is a rare genetic leukodystrophy caused by dominant mutations in the gene coding for the astrocytic intermediate filament protein Glial Fibrillary Acidic Protein (GFAP). Understanding disease mechanisms is complicated by the fact that mutant GFAP promotes further GFAP accumulation, making it difficult to distinguish mutation-specific effects from those caused by elevated GFAP levels. Here, we performed mass spectrometry-based single cell proteomics to investigate proteomic alterations associated with increasing levels of wildtype GFAP and a common AxD-causing mutant GFAP R239C. By analyzing individual cells spanning a broad range of GFAP expression levels, we separated dosage-dependent effects from mutation-specific responses. Cells expressing high levels of wildtype GFAP increasingly resembled R239C-expressing cells at the proteomic level, supporting a role for GFAP accumulation in disease pathogenesis. In contrast, mutant GFAP specifically correlated with increased mitochondrial antioxidant enzymes and remodeling of the proteasome tailored toward ATP- and ubiquitin-independent degradation of oxidized proteins. Integration with proteomics data from patient-derived cortical organoids revealed increased abundance of nuclear-encoded mitochondrial proteins and respiratory chain assembly factors without corresponding changes in mitochondrially encoded proteins, suggesting impaired electron transport chain (ETC) assembly. Consistent with this, AxD cells displayed reduced oxygen consumption, increased glycolytic activity, enhanced utilization of the cytosolic part of the glycerol-3-phosphate (G3P) shuttle, and accumulation of triacylglycerides and lipid droplets. We propose that ETC dysfunction promotes partial uncoupling of the G3P shuttle, allowing sustained regeneration of cytosolic NAD to support glycolysis while diverting G3P toward lipid synthesis and storage. By regenerating NAD through the G3P shuttle rather than lactate fermentation, AxD astrocytes may sustain glycolytic flux while preserving lactate production, an important metabolic substrate for neighboring neurons. Together, our findings identify ETC dysfunction as a central feature of AxD and suggest that metabolic adaptation through the G3P shuttle links mitochondrial dysfunction to glycolytic reprogramming and lipid accumulation. More broadly, these results provide new insight into how astrocyte dysfunction drives molecular pathways implicated in neurodegeneration.

last_author.name: Burgering, B. M.

preprints.title: Systematic mapping of enhancers, silencers, and topological elements with prime editing deletion screens
preprints.abstract: Noncoding regulatory elements in the human genome can control gene expression through distinct mechanisms, including acting as enhancers, silencers, or topological elements. However, we lack tools to identify all such classes systematically and quantify their effects on gene expression in an endogenous genomic context. Here we develop Swap-seq, a method that combines pooled twin prime editing with flow-sorting to delete hundreds of endogenous regulatory sequences and measure their quantitative effects on the expression of a nearby gene. We apply Swap-seq to dissect the regulatory elements that control PPIF expression in THP-1 monocytes. We quantify the effects of distal and intronic enhancers, characterize CTCF insulators, and discover a silencer that regulates distal genes through histone deacetylase (HDAC)-mediated repression of neighboring enhancers. Hundreds of other genomic elements share its chromatin signatures and transcription factor binding sites, suggesting that this silencer represents a broader class of repressive elements. We leverage Swap-seq data to benchmark sequence-to-function models and show that they often capture the local activity of regulatory elements but fail to link them to distal target genes. Swap-seq thus provides a generalizable tool to discover regulatory elements across mechanistic classes, characterize their effects on gene expression, and generate large-scale datasets for evaluating sequence-to-function models.

preprints.title: TBX3 is required for the differentiation of a subset of retinal ganglion and cone photoreceptor cells
preprints.abstract: Retinogenesis is a key step driving the formation of the neurons that later coordinate angiogenesis in the retina. Understanding these complex interactions requires dissecting apart its cellular and molecular drivers. To tease apart the molecular links coupling retinogenesis to vascular development, we utilized conditional knockout mouse models to selectively delete the transcription factor T-box 3 (Tbx3) in 1) astrocytes, 2) postnatal retinal ganglion cells (RGCs), or 3) retinal progenitors. We demonstrate that the hypovascular retina phenotype observed upon Tbx3 loss most likely stems from a disruption of early retinogenesis. Embryonic analyses revealed that TBX3 is required during a critical retinogenic window coinciding with ATOH7 activity. While ATOH7+ progenitors are more abundant in Tbx3 mutants, the expression of key RGC and cone precursor factors (including TBX5, RXRgamma, ISL1/2, POU4F2, SHH, LHX4 and OTX2) is severely diminished, halting proper RGC and cone differentiation. Utilizing birthdating experiments and developmental immunostaining, we establish TBX3 as a novel upstream regulator of RGC and cone photoreceptor specification. Because the degeneration of RGCs is the definitive hallmark of diseases like glaucoma, identifying TBX3 as a driver of early RGC formation positions it as a promising new candidate biomarker for early-stage glaucoma diagnosis and potentially therapeutic targeting.

last_author.name: Viczian, A. S.

preprints.title: Targeting Cardiac Fibrosis with Chimeric Antigen Receptor Neutrophils Derived from Human Pluripotent Stem Cells
preprints.abstract: Heart failure remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, with cardiac fibrosis contributing to disease progression. Following myocardial injury, activated cardiac fibroblasts orchestrate adverse extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, which leads to tissue stiffening and compromised contractility. Despite the clinical importance of cardiac fibrosis, current pharmacological interventions modulate disease progression without directly eliminating activated fibrogenic cells. To target these cells directly, we engineered human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC)-derived neutrophils expressing a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) directed against fibroblast activation protein (FAP). In vitro, FAP CAR neutrophils exhibited increased reactive oxygen species-associated fluorescence during fibroblast co-culture and dose-dependent cytotoxicity in 2D cultures, while reducing fibroblast-associated fluorescence in 3D cardiac organoids without a significant reduction in cardiomyocyte-associated cardiac troponin T staining. FAP CAR neutrophils also showed increased iNOS and decreased Arginase-1 expression compared with unmodified neutrophils, consistent with a shift toward an N1-associated polarization profile. Analysis of public cardiac single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-sequencing datasets identified temporal patterns of immune-associated expression and fibroblast activation that informed treatment timing. In a murine myocardial infarction (MI) model, mice treated systemically with FAP CAR neutrophils showed higher day 7 left ventricular ejection fraction than PBS-treated mice in an exploratory comparison. Together, these findings support further evaluation of hPSC-derived FAP CAR neutrophils as an immunotherapeutic approach to cardiac fibrosis.

preprints.title: The Core Promoter has an active role in interpreting patterning information
preprints.abstract: Precise spatiotemporal control of gene expression is conventionally attributed to distal enhancers. The extent to which different core promoters actively shape transcriptional output from enhancers remains unclear, especially in the context of genes that contain alternate promoters. We have explored these questions using the Drosophila grainy head (grh) locus, and tested the activities conferred by its alternate promoters in combination with a well characterised Notch responsive enhancer. We find that, of the alternate promoters tested, only the grh short promoter is competent to drive neuroblast-specific expression. Notably, when paired with identical enhancers, grh-short and grh-medium promoters drive distinct expression patterns. The activity of other core promoters, such as hsp70, is also selective. Together the results establish that the core promoter acts alongside enhancers to confer specificity and robustness on gene expression profiles.

preprints.title: Transient transcriptomic rejuvenation during intestinal and liver regeneration in mice
preprints.abstract: Aging and regeneration are fundamental biological processes, but the relationship between them is poorly understood. During intestinal regeneration, adult epithelial cells reactivate developmental programs that support repair. To investigate if this plasticity alters tissue biological age, we developed and validated intestinal tissue and epithelium-specific transcriptomic aging clocks. Across various regeneration models, epithelial states were predicted by these clocks to be younger than controls. Their expression changes were also negatively associated with intestinal aging signatures. The resulting younger state was characterized by YAP-associated regeneration and reduced mature enterocyte identity. In a separate irradiation model, the predicted epithelial age first increased, then fell at the peak of regeneration and later increased again during recovery. The pace of this response differed with host age. In a chemotherapy-induced injury model, epithelium in young animals also entered this younger state earlier and then returned to its preinjury state during recovery. Old epithelium responded later, but also reversibly transitioned through a rejuvenated state. Further spatial transcriptomic analyses linked lower epithelial age with regeneration in selected injured and tumor-associated regions. In addition, liver regeneration after partial hepatectomy in old animals also led to a decreased transcriptomic age, accompanied by pathway changes negatively associated with aging signatures. Overall, these findings suggest that mammalian regeneration is associated with a transient reduction in biological age, whose timing and persistence depend on tissue, host age and the course of repair.

preprints.title: Tumour-stroma signaling drives a reversible program with neural-like features in cancer-associated fibroblasts
preprints.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is one of the most aggressive cancers, in part due to a dense and highly plastic tumor microenvironment dominated by cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs). In previous work, we identified a CAF population expressing a neural-associated NES+SOX4+NOTCH1+ program that increased with disease progression. The signals driving this state and the mechanisms regulating it remained unclear. Here, we investigated how tumor-derived signals activate this program and whether it represents a stable fibroblast identity or a reversible state. Using spatial transcriptomic data spanning normal pancreas to invasive carcinoma, we identified EGF, FGF2 and BDNF as candidate tumor-to-fibroblast signals associated with disease progression. Functional experiments in patient-derived CAFs and human fibroblast cell lines showed that EGF and FGF2 are sufficient to induce the NES+SOX4+NOTCH1+ program. Growth factor withdrawal reversed the NES+SOX4+NOTCH1+ program at both the protein and transcriptional levels, indicating that this state is dynamic and environment dependent. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis further revealed a multi-phase response involving early loss of fibroblast-associated features, transient activation of neural-associated genes, and a later stress-associated state. Regulatory analyses identified ETS-family transcription factors as key regulators of the program, while phosphoproteomic profiling and inhibitor studies showed that MAPK/ERK signaling plays a central role in its transcriptional activation. Finally, pan-cancer single-cell analysis showed that this state is enriched in CAFs and increases from normal to tumor tissue across multiple cancer types. Together, these findings define a reversible, growth factor-driven CAF program and identify signaling mechanisms that may provide opportunities to selectively modulate tumor-supportive fibroblast states.

preprints.title: 2C-RT Quantifies Genome-Wide DNA Replication Perturbationsand Redefines RIF1-CDC7 Regulation of Replication Timing
preprints.abstract: Replication timing (RT) coordinates DNA synthesis with genome organization and influences mutation rates, cancer evolution, and developmental plasticity. Current methods infer S-phase timing from DNA content, an assumption that obscures responses to replication perturbations and limits accurate comparisons of RT changes. Here, we develop 2C-RT, a multiplexed sequencing approach that uses DNA content-independent markers for robust RT profiling across S phase. Combining 2C-RT with imaging, we resolve distinct layers of human RT control and identify local and genome-wide responses to drugs and genetic perturbations. We find that RIF1 spatially restricts CDC7 activity and that its loss does not neutralize RT per se but advances replication across most RIF1-sensitive regions. A conserved MCM5 bob1 mutation lowers the origin-activation threshold and reveals a role for CDC7 in establishing local origin dominance. These findings support a revised model in which CDC7 primes early origins, CDK promotes permissive origin firing genome-wide, and RIF1 counteracts CDC7 in distinct chromatin states and peripheral nuclear domains.

preprints.title: A High-Content Pseudotime Framework for Morphological Profiling of Dengue Virus Inhibitors from a Drug-Repurposing Library
preprints.abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) causes dengue fever, a globally prevalent, epidemic-prone disease with no FDA-approved antivirals. Additionally, the available vaccine for DENV can increase the risk of severe dengue fever for those who have never had a DENV infection due to antibody-dependent enhancement. Thus, there is an urgent need to identify DENV antivirals. Drug repurposing, high-content screening, and machine learning were leveraged to efficiently identify antivirals likely to inhibit DENV replication. Using high-content screening in a DENV infection model, we characterized the morphological patterns of NS4B and envelope (E) protein expression over time and developed a viral pseudotime model that predicts infection progression to aid in phenotypic interpretation of drug effects. We then developed a single cell infection classifier for antiviral efficacy and performed high-throughput drug screening of 960 compounds. We identified four concentration-dependent inhibitors of DENV with nanomolar-to-submicromolar potencies: esomeprazole, GW4064, pralatrexate, and LY411575. With our pseudotime machine learning model trained on data from the time-series assay, we scored the concentration-dependent inhibitors to map their mechanism of action onto time points in the viral life cycle. Our most notable results show that LY411575, a gamma secretase inhibitor, exhibited an IC of 72 nM and reduced percent infection to near the level of the mock infection control. Pseudotime inferences generated mechanistic predictions that were supported by time-of-addition experiments, indicating that LY411575 arrests DENV infection before the development of late-stage infection associated morphologies, while retaining activity when added after inoculation.

last_author.name: O'Meara, M. J.

preprints.title: A Novel Role for FSTL-1 in Hematopoietic Stem Cell Homeostasis and Post-injury Regeneration
preprints.abstract: Background: The ability to repopulate all lineages of blood cells from a single hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) requires a constant balancing between maintenance of quiescence/self-renewal and the need for differentiation and adoption of specific lineage phenotypes. A classical interpretation suggests that during homeostasis, long- and then short-term HSCs differentiate into multipotent progenitors (MPPs), which then lack self-renewal capacity but can still differentiate into all downstream lineages. While much is known about the intrinsic and extrinsic regulators that promote HSC homeostasis, less is known about factors which influence HSC behavior following significant bone marrow (BM) injury, such as sublethal irradiation (SLI). Methods: Conditional knock-out of follistatin-like 1 (FSTL-1) was achieved by breeding mice with floxed Fstl1 sites to mice expressing CreERT2 under control of the ROSA locus, followed by systemic tamoxifen administration. ELISA and RT-PCR quantitated protein and RNA level loss of FSTL-1, respectively. HSC populations were assessed by flow cytometry under multiple conditions. Sublethal irradiation induced BM injury and blocking polyclonal FSTL-1 antibodies were used to recapitulate results seen with genetic ablation. Finally, single cell RNA sequencing defined both cell-specific expression of Fstl1 within the BM compartment, but also identified transcripts and pathways upregulated in the absence of FSTL-1. Results: These studies delineate a novel role for FSTL-1 in regulating HSC biology. In addition to selective expression of Fstl1 within HSCs, genetic deletion of Fstl1 increases Lineage negative;Sca-1+c-Kit+ (LSK) cell number and alters HSC homeostasis. These findings are further amplified in the BM in the context of recovery from sublethal irradiation. Importantly, the post-irradiation increase in BM cellularity seen with Fstl1 deletion is replicated by treatment with anti-FSTL-1 polyclonal antibodies. Finally, single cell RNA sequencing reveals distinct Fstl1 expression in specific LSK subpopulations, including HSCs and proliferating cells, and identifies a novel relationship between decreased FSTL-1 levels and enrichment of canonical metabolic pathways including oxidative phosphorylation, fatty acid metabolism, and glycolysis. Conclusions: Taken together, these results highlight a novel role for FSTL-1 in promoting HSC homeostasis. They also unlock an innovative way to promote HSPC recovery following BM injury, knowledge predicted to be of significant therapeutic value.

preprints.title: A rapid, genetically-tractable human iPSC-derived model for studying tissue-resident macrophage biology in Alzheimer's and other diseases
preprints.abstract: Large-scale genetic and preclinical studies strongly implicate myeloid cells, particularly brain-resident macrophages, in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Efferocytic clearance of apoptotic cells and other cholesterol-rich cellular debris is a core macrophage function and represents an active area of AD research. However, human tissue-resident macrophages remain difficult to model in vitro as they acquire their transcriptional and functional identities in response to signals from their host tissue microenvironment. Many existing differentiation protocols mimic human brain macrophage developmental trajectories, but these protocols rely either on multi-step cytokine cocktails and lengthy differentiation or transduction of multiple transcription factors, both of which introduce variability and complicate genetic manipulation. To address these limitations, we developed a simplified protocol that generates high-purity (>90% CD45+CD11b+) human iPSC-derived macrophage-like cells (iMacs) from cryopreservable erythro-myeloid progenitor (EMP)-like intermediates in 19 days, including a final 7-day maturation step driven by macrophage colony-stimulating factor (M-CSF) alone. Transcriptomic profiling reveals that iMacs show enrichment for phagocytic and lysosomal programs, processes integral to efferocytosis. At both the transcriptional and protein level, iMacs have higher expression of scavenger receptors such as CD36, CD163 and MRC1, and of AD risk genes such as TREM2. Functionally, iMacs show enhanced phagocytic uptake of diverse substrates relative to iPSC-derived microglia, including carboxylated latex beads, zymosan, amyloid-{beta} 1-42, and amyloid-{beta} 1-40, and exhibit expanded lysosomal mass. Robust TREM2 expression and signaling make iMacs a sensitive platform for interrogating TREM2 biology, with markedly higher phosphorylation of SYK and PLC{gamma}2 in response to TREM2 engagement compared to iPSC-derived microglia. iMacs also tolerate lipid-mediated siRNA transfection with high survival and knockdown efficiency, enabling rapid genetic perturbation of AD risk genes. Together, these features make iMacs a practical, scalable, and genetically tractable human macrophage model for studying the regulation and cell biology of core macrophage functions that are known to play critical roles in AD, aging, and other disorders.

preprints.title: A versatile set of computational tools for inference of genetic ancestry from human molecular data
preprints.abstract: Molecular properties of human diseases and conditions often exhibit dependence on the genetic ancestry of the donor. In order to make more human molecular data available for ancestry-informed research, we developed a set of software tools termed Robust Ancestry Inference using Data Synthesis (RAIDS) for inference of genetic ancestry from sequence data that pose challenges to genotyping. Here we describe a recent expansion and refinement of RAIDS, applicable to nucleic-acid sequence data resultant from a broad range of experimental strategies. These strategies currently include whole-genome, whole-exome, and targeted gene panel sequencing, RNA-Seq, including single-cell RNA-Seq, chromatin-accessibility (ATAC-Seq), and protein-binding (ChIP-Seq) assays. RAIDS inferential tools perform robustly in the presence of somatic nucleic-acid alterations caused by cancer and under the conditions of extreme non-uniformity of sequence read coverage, yielding both global ancestry and ancestral admixtures of the donor. RAIDS is available as an eponymous Bioconductor package.

last_author.affiliation: CSHL

preprints.title: Alignment-Aware Genomic Coordinate Encoding for Long-Range DNA Modeling
preprints.abstract: Existing genomic foundation models (GFMs) are adept at capturing local, sequential dependencies in DNA. However, their architectures often struggle to efficiently model gene regulation features, such as sparse motifs and distal regulatory elements that operate beyond linear proximity. Moreover, standard positional encodings fail to fully exploit the reference genome coordinate system. Therefore, we present USM-AA, an alignment-aware genomic foundation model that incorporates reference genome coordinates through a non-contiguous positional encoding, Alignment-Aware Rotary Position Embedding, and an alignment embedding module encoding chromosome, strand, and Compact Idiosyncratic Gapped Alignment Report (CIGAR) information. To improve long-range sequence modeling, USM-AA leverages a reverse-complement masked learning strategy. Pretrained on alignment-aware genomic sequences spanning cross-species evolution and human population variation, USM-AA consistently outperforms existing models across multiple downstream tasks, highlighting the importance of alignment-aware representations for genomic sequence modeling.

preprints.title: An AI-Enabled Translational Drug Discovery Framework for NALCN Channelopathy: From High-Throughput Screening to Therapeutic Candidate
preprints.abstract: Background: More than 90% of rare diseases lack an approved therapy, partly reflecting economic barriers in developing treatments for small patient populations. A common bottleneck is costly and resource-intensive hit-to-lead prioritization. Congenital contractures of the limbs and face, hypotonia, and developmental delay (CLIFAHDD) is an ultra-rare neurodevelopmental disease often caused by de novo gain-of-function variants in the sodium leak channel NALCN, with no approved treatments. Methods: We developed a cost and resource-efficient, AI-enabled translational drug discovery framework integrating phenotypic high-throughput screening (HTS), structural biology foundation models for hit-to-lead prioritization, and orthogonal experimental validation. We applied this framework for drug repurposing to identify NALCN inhibitors as therapeutic candidates for CLIFAHDD. We screened ~1,200 approved drugs using a fluorescence-based membrane potential assay in doxycycline-inducible HEK293 cells stably expressing the NALCN channelosome. Boltz-2 modeling predicted binding affinity and mode to prioritize hits. Lead repurposing candidates were selected by a multidisciplinary expert review panel. Lead candidates were evaluated using patch-clamp electrophysiology in HEK293 cells expressing wild-type or CLIFAHDD-associated NALCN variants, primary mouse hippocampal neurons, and a C. elegans NALCN gain-of-function model. Results: HTS identified 11 candidate NALCN inhibitors. Boltz-2 prioritized candidates based on predicted binding affinity and predicted binding within the NALCN pore, consistent with a direct pore-blocking mechanism. Aprepitant emerged as the lead candidate after multidisciplinary evaluation based on its predicted mechanism, pharmacologic properties, blood-brain barrier penetration, established safety profile, and regulatory approval in children and adults. Patch-clamp electrophysiology confirmed partial inhibition of NALCN-mediated sodium leak currents in HEK293 cells (IC50;=2.22 M), with comparable potency against Cav3.1 (IC50=1.63 M). In primary mouse hippocampal neurons, aprepitant reduced sodium leak currents, hyperpolarized resting membrane potential, and decreased spontaneous firing. Aprepitant rescued hyperlocomotor and dystonic phenotypes in a C. elegans gain-of-function NALCN model. There was notable concordance between AI-predicted hits, phenotypic screening hits, and experimental validation. Conclusion: These findings identify aprepitant as a lead therapeutic candidate for CLIFAHDD, and establish an AI-enabled translational drug discovery framework integrating phenotypic screening, structural modeling, and experimental validation for NALCN channelopathies. This scalable and resource-conscious strategy may accelerate hit-to-lead prioritization and drug discovery for rare and ultra-rare diseases lacking effective therapies.

preprints.title: Artificial Intelligence Applied to Epigenomic Data in Leukemia: A Systematic Review of Diagnostic, Prognostic and Monitoring Models
preprints.abstract: Background: Epigenetic deregulation is a defining feature of leukemia, and DNA methylation and chromatin accessibility profiles encode the cell of origin, lineage and clinical behaviour of the disease. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) can extract predictive patterns from these high-dimensional data, but the published models have not been systematically appraised. We systematically reviewed AI models built on epigenomic data in leukemia for diagnosis, prognosis, relapse and treatment-response prediction, and measurable residual disease (MRD) detection. Methods: This review followed PRISMA 2020 and the SWiM guideline. PubMed was searched on 7 October 2026 with three structured queries, supplemented by a broader PubMed query, citation searching and web searching. Eligible studies were peer-reviewed primary studies that applied an ML or deep-learning algorithm to DNA methylation, chromatin-accessibility or histone-modification data from human leukemia samples and reported a quantitative diagnostic, prognostic, response or MRD outcome. Risk of bias and applicability were assessed with PROBAST, informed by PROBAST+AI. Owing to heterogeneity, results were synthesized narratively and in structured tables, without meta-analysis. Results: Of 68 unique database records and 32 reports from other sources, 30 studies (2010-2026; 22 since 2020) were included: 16 in acute myeloid leukemia, 4 in acute lymphoblastic leukemia, 2 spanning acute leukemia lineages, 3 in juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia and 5 in chronic lymphocytic leukemia; 10 were pediatric. DNA methylation was the input in 28 studies and chromatin accessibility in 2; no eligible study modelled histone marks. Tree ensembles (n = 9) and support vector machines (n = 5) were the most frequent algorithms. Diagnostic classifiers reported accuracy, concordance or F1 scores of 0.87-1.00, and two classifiers were applied to nanopore sequencing data, one returning acute leukemia subtype calls within about 2 hours. Prognostic epigenomic scores were associated with survival (reported hazard ratios 2.36-10.82), but discrimination fell on transport to independent cohorts (C-index 0.677 internally vs 0.529 in one external cohort). Fifteen studies validated models on an external epigenomic cohort, one prospectively. Overall risk of bias was high in 21 studies, unclear in 8 and low in 1, driven by the analysis domain (small samples, absent calibration, possible data leakage). Calibration was reported in 3 studies and code was available for 11. Conclusions: Epigenomic AI models classify leukemia subtypes with high reported accuracy and can deliver same-day diagnoses, and methylation-based scores add prognostic information. However, the evidence is dominated by retrospective, high-risk-of-bias development studies with limited external validation and almost no prospective or impact evaluation. Prospective, multi-center validation with calibrated, transparently reported models is required before clinical adoption.

preprints.title: Benchmarking single-cell foundation models reveals an advantage in the low-data regime for cell-type and disease-state prediction
preprints.abstract: Single-cell foundation models perform well on cell-type classification, but their value for disease-state prediction and their advantage over classical representations remains unclear. We benchmarked cell-representations from four foundation models using logistic regression, on 868 disease-prediction tasks (82 datasets) and 65 cell-type datasets from CELLxGENE. With full data, the baseline (log-normalized counts) outperformed the best model (TranscriptFormer-Sapiens) for cell type and matched it for disease. However, with few labeled cells, TranscriptFormer-Sapiens significantly outperformed the baseline in both tasks up to ~102 samples per class. Our comprehensive zero-shot benchmark identifies the data-scarce regime as a domain where Single-cell foundation models truly show advantage.
